Thus far, 2026 has been chastening for the fallen giants of world football. For Italy, it has been the year of Bosnia and Herzegovina and Bodo/Glimt, the Balkan team meaning a third consecutive World Cup took place without the Azzurri, the Norwegian side eliminating Inter Milan from the Champions League. There were other indications of decline – a Champions League table with the reigning Scudetto winners Napoli in 30th or Italy’s sole representatives in the last 16, Atalanta, going down 10-2 on aggregate to Bayern Munich – and they combined to paint a bleak picture.

So if Serie A returns with the sense its best days are behind it, some of its historic forces have the same feel. And yet that provided some of the drama last season: two of Italy’s three most decorated clubs, AC Milan and Juventus, spurned promising positions to miss out on Champions League qualification. They will instead be the biggest clubs in the Europa League after being leapfrogged by Cesc Fabregas’ insurgents from Como. The third of Italy’s traditional powers, Inter, cruised to their 21st Scudetto in Cristian Chivu’s first campaign in charge; equalling his predecessor Simone Inzaghi’s total of Serie A titles was at least compensation for faring far worse in Europe.

His rivals this year are set to be a mixture of the familiar, with Serie A’s capacity to recycle its managers, and an intriguing newcomer. A division where clubs have been starved of funds features two expensive arrivals from Paris St-Germain, charged with bringing goals to the underachievers, and a further influx of English defenders.

Chivu will share San Siro with Ruben Amorim who, in the way Serie A’s fortunes have nosedived, seemed the man AC Milan ended up with rather than perhaps wanted, given interest in Oliver Glasner and Andoni Iraola. It is nevertheless an opportunity the Portuguese did not earn with his wretched spell in charge of Manchester United.

He will presumably import his flagship 3-4-3; whether Luka Modric, who turns 41 next month, wants to be in a central-midfield duo remains to be seen but Milan have backed Amorim by allowing him to make the biggest signing in the Serie A summer: his fellow Portuguese Goncalo Ramos for a club record €74m (£63.3m). It at least should ensure wingers Rafael Leao and Christian Pulisic are no longer an ersatz strike duo, even if Amorim’s record with centre-forwards was better in Portugal than England.

open image in gallery Goncalo Ramos is the big-money signing of the summer ( Reuters )

open image in gallery Randal Kolo Muani spearheads a new-look Juventus attack ( Getty )

Ramos was liberated from the PSG bench. He used to be joined there, before an unsuccessful loan at Tottenham, by Randal Kolo Muani, who has returned to Juventus, another to borrow him before. A potential €50m (£42.8m) fee means he has to spearhead a new-look attack, with the younger talents of Kenan Yildiz and Kerim Alajbegovic, a €32m (£27.4m) arrival from Bayer Leverkusen. Luciano Spalletti, who walked into a struggling side when Igor Tudor was sacked, is reshaping his forward line with Dusan Vlahovic going after an underwhelming and expensive spell and after last year’s striking additions Jonathan David and Lois Openda struggled.

Inter, meanwhile, already had the capocannoniere last season, Lautaro Martinez, and the player with most assists, the division’s MVP Federico Dimarco. The presence of players at their peak allows Chivu to continue his task of making the nerazzurri younger. Buying back his old teammate Dejan Stankovic’s son Aleksandar is a nod to a Champions League-winning past. Four of Inzaghi’s veterans are gone, in Francesco Acerbi, Matteo Darmian, Yann Sommer and Stefan de Vrij, who have a combined age of 146. The buccaneering wing-back Denzel Dumfries, who has joined Real Madrid, may be the greatest loss of the departures. Djed Spence, less of a goalscorer but fresh from a remarkable World Cup, makes for a different replacement.

open image in gallery Como manager Cesc Fabregas during a pre-season friendly against Liverpool ( Getty )

Even with Spence, Inter’s defence may not be that youthful next season. Signing John Stones, and reuniting him with Manuel Akanji, gives them a player who should suit the pace of play as well as Chivu’s 3-5-2. It also provides Thomas Tuchel with reasons to visit Italy on defensive scouting trips, with Trevoh Chalobah moving to Como, though it remains to be seen if Fikayo Tomori, potentially the latest in the list of players exiled by Amorim, will still be at AC Milan.

At Como, Fabregas has also kept the precocious Nico Paz, though Real Madrid retain an option to buy the playmaker back. A challenge for the Spaniard will be to juggle domestic and European football. Roma, propelled by the goals of the mid-season arrival Donyell Malan, will join them in the Champions League. Gian Piero Gasperini, who won his power struggle with Claudio Ranieri, has further bolstered his attack with the €35m (£30m) signing of Bologna’s Santiago Castro, while Portuguese wonder kid Rodrigo Mora brings more potential to the Eternal City.

open image in gallery Djed Spence arrives at Inter after a fine showing at the World Cup ( Getty )

Napoli’s big summer striking signing was one set up last summer: Rasmus Hojlund, after a successful loan, and his purchase triggered now. An issue for new manager Massimiliano Allegri, however, is that his predecessor Antonio Conte’s capacity to spend big meant much of his transfer budget was already committed. Though Romelu Lukaku is gone to Fenerbahce, Allegri, sacked by Milan, will have to use many of his predecessor’s players, Scott McTominay and Kevin De Bruyne among them, in his search for his seventh Scudetto. That the sixth came back in 2019 suggests he is in decline; Napoli may be too.

But Serie A can specialise in finding new homes for its familiar faces on the managerial merry-go-round. Maurizio Sarri, who left Lazio for a second time, is now at Atalanta, and shorn of the Chelsea-bound Marco Palestra. Ivan Juric, who joined the Bergamo club last year, is now at promoted Monza; it may not bode well that his last three jobs have only spanned 12, 16 and 15 games respectively.

open image in gallery Ruben Amorim will rebuild his reputation in Italy after a torrid spell with Man Utd ( Reuters )

There are reminders of the happier days when Italy were World Cup winners; of the 2006 team, Gennaro Gattuso is now manager of Lazio, replacing Sarri, and Fabio Grosso has joined Fiorentina, who have moved on from Paolo Vanoli, even though he kept a team who failed to win in their first 15 games up. They should not be in a second successive relegation battle: the Viola have spent heavily and also borrowed Franco Mastantuono from Real Madrid.

That seven different clubs have finished in the top four in the last three seasons can offer encouragement to the ambitious. That Inter look overwhelming favourites suggests the battle for fourth could be contested more than the one for first; Juventus may be their closest challengers. But while Serie A can be compelling in itself, its standing and self-esteem will depend in part on results against outsiders. The Italians could do with making the right kind of impression in Europe again.

So you’ve got the grades, now you’re off to university. But before you stock up on Pukka Pads, reMarkable is giving students a reason to go digital, with the brand slashing prices on its ever-popular digital notebooks.

Designed to feel like putting pen to paper, reMarkable’s tablets let you scribble down lecture notes, annotate documents and convert your handwritten text into digital text for easy organisation.

Right now, reMarkable has slashed £100 off some of its digital notebook bundles. With the offer running for the next two weeks, you can save on the reMarkable paper pro and smaller paper pro move. Kicking off today (20 August) the deal will end on 1 September, so you’ve got time to grab a bargain before Fresher’s Week.

open image in gallery ( Thomas Deehan/The Independent )

You can currently save £100 on this bundle, bringing the price down to just £399. With this bundle, you get the pocket-sized digital notebook, the brand’s premium marker stylus and a standard folio, giving you everything you need to start scribbling straight out of the box.

In his review of the paper pro move, IndyBest tester Thomas Deehan dubbed the device as the best digital notebook for writers. “The paper pro move is effectively a shrunk-down paper pro with all the features intact,” he said. “You have an E Ink-style display that’s capable of producing colour, and a backlight that makes scribbling down notes after dark an easy process.”

If you’d prefer something more luxe, you can get the same bundle but with a leather ‘folio premium’ rather than a regular ‘folio standard’ with a discount of £100, dropping the price to just £429.

open image in gallery ( Thomas Deehan/The Independent )

If you want a bit more space to write, you can also save £100 on the larger reMarkable paper pro bundle. You get the 11.8in digital notebook, the marker premium stylus and a standard folio. The paper pro has a much larger colour display and adjustable reading light.

In his review of the paper pro, IndyBest tester Thomas Deehan named it the best premium digital notebook. “This larger tablet doubles down on everything that made its predecessor great, by boasting a larger 11.8in display that offers more room to scribble down your thoughts, alongside a colour display,” he said, while also praising the two-week battery life.

If you want an upgraded case, the paper pro bundle with the marker premium and folio premium has also been slashed in price, from £729 to £629. As with the paper pro move deal above, you get the same digital notebook and stylus, as well as reMarkable’s more premium leather case.

Finally, there’s a deal for anyone who wants to ditch their laptop entirely – not just their paper notepads. The paper pro bundle with the marker premium and type folio has been slashed from £769 to £669. The type folio case includes a physical keyboard for the paper pro, letting you type directly on the tablet when you’ve had enough of writing by hand.

News.title: Robinson demolishes Pakistan to cement importance to new regime
News.content:
He also has that edge, the grunt of an angry fast bowler, and his competitiveness was just what Root needed considering his other quicks were still in Hundred mode. Archer bowled too short, Gus Atkinson grew into the innings but was wicketless and it took a while for Tongue to click, although once he did he was unplayable against the right-handers with his pace and angle.

Robinson’s lack of pace gives them the keeper-standing-up option. It worked a treat when he bowled Pakistan’s top-scorer, Abdullah Shafique for 61, his footwork messed up by Jamie Smith breathing down his neck.

Pakistan would have batted first had they won the toss and it is a good pitch that will improve as the Test goes on, although with rain around all week the overheads will have a say on the game. Pakistan have far more recent red-ball exposure than England’s batsmen but they were ill-equipped to deal with Robinson and Tongue.

Most supporters were still walking into the ground when the former struck first ball, Azan Awais lbw to a nip-backer. Shan Masood’s stilted footwork was ripe for exposing and Robinson’s first ball over the wicket to the left-hander was full and straight to beat the loose drive.

Imam-ul-Haq had done the hard work, seeing off Robinson only to flash a drive to second slip off a wide ball from Tongue to end Pakistan’s only stand of substance of the innings: 93 for the third wicket.

Robinson cracked the innings open further with Saud Shakeel leg before, who was too slow to call for the review that would have saved him. Hawk-Eye showed the ball would have gone over the top.

Robinson then bowled Shafique in his next over and Pakistan were toppling. Tongue cranked up the pace, bowled full and the perpendicular angle into the right-handers did the rest.

News.title: Burnham blames Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation
News.content:
Andy Burnham has blamed Donald Trump’s war in Iran for higher inflation in Britain.

Inflation jumped from 2.6pc in June to 2.9pc last month, according to the Office for National Statistics, threatening to undermine Mr Burnham’s pledge to bring down the cost of living.

The Prime Minister said: “We can’t control though what is going on in the Middle East and the effect of the conflict there is now being felt in inflation here, and in other countries around the world.

“I realise these times are really hard but already people can see a month into office I have done things that will make a difference.”

July’s inflation figure was affected by a 13.5pc rise in the Ofgem price cap in response to the energy crisis unleashed by the Iran war. It means prices are now rising at their highest rate since March.

The latest figure shows the struggle that Mr Burnham faces to fulfil his promise to bring down living costs.

There are fears that inflation will climb higher in the coming months as the impact of the conflict filters through to the economy.

Speaking at an event in the North East, Mr Burnham added: “I want to lead a cost-of-living Government, and I’ve already taken steps as Prime Minister to show I will help people wherever I can. I can’t do everything, I think people know that.

“We’re in tough times, but where I can do something to make life that little bit better, I will do it.”

Since arriving in No 10, Mr Burnham has made tackling the cost of living a key policy focus.

The Prime Minister announced last month that he would remove VAT from electricity bills from October and reinstate the £2 cap on bus fares from next year.

However, average energy bills are expected to jump by around 4pc from October, according to energy analysts Cornwall Insight, wiping out any potential savings from Mr Burnham’s VAT cut.

The analysts said Ofgem’s price cap – which limits the average annual energy bill faced by a family home – would rise from £1,663 to £1,729.

Despite concerns about increasing gas and electricity bills, July’s rate of inflation was in line with economists’ expectations.

Money markets now expect policymakers at the Bank of England to hold interest rates at 3.75pc at their next meeting in September.

News.title: Unemployment rate fails to fall for Burnham
News.content:
An expected drop in the unemployment rate has failed to materialise, dealing a setback to Andy Burnham’s hopes of reviving Britain’s ailing economy.

Unemployment remained stuck at 4.9pc in the three months to June, while the number of payrolled employees fell by 13,000, according to figures from the Office for National Statistics. Economists had predicted that the unemployment rate would ease to 4.8pc.

While the three-month figure was flat, monthly data showed a sharp increase at the end of the period. Unemployment jumped to 5.4pc in June, up from 4.6pc the previous month.

That marked the highest reading since October 2020 and the biggest monthly jump in 13 years.

Julian Jessop, at the Institute of Economic Affairs, described the latest jobs figures as “dire”.

He said: “The unemployment rate remains stubbornly high, with a big jump in the single month figure for June.”

It came as private sector wage growth slumped to a six-year low of just 2.8pc. That stands in contrast to a 6.1pc pay increase for the average public sector worker in the same period.

Meanwhile, vacancies dropped to 707,000 in the three months to July – the lowest level since 2021 – with a particular strain on entry-level job openings.

Ben Harrison, director of the Work Foundation at Lancaster University, warned that the UK was “trapped in a deepening jobs drought”.

Thomas Pugh, chief economist at RSM UK, said: “Stagnant, or even negative, real wage growth in the second half of this year will intensify the pressure on Burnham and Healey to come up with a package to support the cost of living.

“However, doing anything substantial without breaching either the fiscal rules or the manifesto commitments looks increasingly difficult given the deterioration in headroom and commitments to spend big on everything from defence to social care.”

News.title: Top British scientist steps down from WHO
News.content:
One of Britain’s best-known scientists has resigned as assistant director-general of the World Health Organization.

Sir Jeremy Farrar became a household name during the pandemic when he served on the UK’s Scientific Advisory Group for Emergencies (Sage).

Sources inside the WHO and the broader scientific community told The Telegraph he resigned his position on Monday.

While it is not clear what prompted his resignation, colleagues told The Telegraph he had been unhappy within the organisation for some time. One speculated that he had become increasingly frustrated with its internal politics and bureaucracy.

Sir Jeremy, 64, who was also a former director of the Wellcome Trust, could not immediately be reached for comment.

The surprise move comes at a difficult time for the WHO, which is undergoing a major restructuring after suffering cuts and a massive funding shortfall following the United States’s withdrawal from it in January. It is also fighting a major outbreak of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, the WHO’s Director-General, announced Dr Farrar’s decision in an email to all staff on Tuesday morning, saying that the British scientist will “retire” from the WHO, effective September 30.

In the email, seen by The Telegraph, Dr Tedros said: “Dr Farrar has demonstrated an exceptional commitment to science and public health at the highest levels, and we are grateful that he chose to bring his experience, energy and conviction to WHO.

“On behalf of the entire organisation, I extend my sincere thanks to Dr Farrar... [and wish] him every success in his next chapter and a well-deserved retirement.”

He added that Dr Bruce Aylward will take over as the new Assistant Director-General for Health Promotion, Disease Prevention and Care.

Sports.title: Hull coach opens up on tragic death of 17-month-old daughter, Ten Hag’s £1,500 gift and taking on his beloved Man Utd
Sports.content:
OLD TRAFFORD season ticket holders never want Manchester United to lose.

But Hull City assistant Dean Holden will again put childhood loyalties aside in Saturday’s Premier League opener.



Holden is a lifelong Red Devils fan and has had an Stretford End season ticket for 34-years – but will be plotting United’s downfall in the rival dugout for Saturday’s Premier League opener.

United have always been central to life for Salford-born Holden, though keeping the newly-promoted Tigers in the top-flight is now his priority.



He previously managed against United when he was Charlton boss for a 2023 League Cup game and was also Bristol City’s No2 when they stunned Jose Mourinho’s United in the same competition in 2017.

Holden explains how he found out about the opening-day meeting, telling SunSport: “I was waiting at home all morning for the fixtures to come out and I had to take our youngest son Chase to school.



“As I got in the car my phone just started to blow up. My dad was ringing and Danielle was at home, my wife with the other kids.

“It was a great moment because it’s a big part of my life is that football club.

“My very first day in the job of being the Charlton manager was the Carabao Cup quarter-final draw when we played United.”

Holden played over 400 EFL matches as a defender for 10 different clubs, many of the years scuppered through injury, but the season ticket has been in his family since 1992.



Fixtures Results Table Arsenal 20:00 Regular Season Coventry Hull 12:30 Regular Season Man Utd Everton 15:00 Regular Season Palace Ipswich 15:00 Regular Season Sunderland Forest 15:00 Regular Season Leeds Brentford 17:30 Regular Season Spurs No results yet P W D L GD Pts 1 Arsenal 0 0 0 0 0 0 2 Villa 0 0 0 0 0 0 3 Bournemouth 0 0 0 0 0 0 4 Brentford 0 0 0 0 0 0 5 Brighton 0 0 0 0 0 0 6 Chelsea 0 0 0 0 0 0 7 Coventry 0 0 0 0 0 0 8 Palace 0 0 0 0 0 0

And his phone has been ringing off the hook with calls for tickets from friends about Hull’s first game back in the top-flight in nine years.

He joked: “I’ve just had people coming out of the woodwork asking for tickets and it’s a nightmare. It’s an absolute nightmare and I’m scrambling.”

Holden previously said United are “in his blood” and he was an Old Trafford ball-boy as a kid.

He told SunSport: “My dad was a steward at Old Trafford and he has taken me around to pretty much every side of that stadium over the years from being a young kid.



“So all my memories of being a kid, of going to games and queuing up overnight for tickets and going around the country watching them.”

When he took his Charlton side to Old Trafford for the last-eight tie almost four years ago, then-manager Erik ten Hag left him a gift after Marcus Rashford’s late double ended any hopes of a cup shock.

His friend later Googled the bottle of red wine gifted by Ten Hag—only to discover it was valued at a whopping £1,500.

He said: “We’ve still not opened that. So that’s going to be one for the kids in the future, hopefully. My kids also got one of Rashford’s signed shirts too.



“I learned a lot from Ten Hag and to get him behind closed doors without any cameras, he was really honest.

“He was extremely kind and generous with his time and his advice. I’m always trying to learn and find new ways of doing things, so he appreciated that.”

Despite the romantic opening-day storyline, Holden is hellbent on helping manager Sergej Jakirovic keep Hull in the top flight, reminding the squad to look at the long haul.

Holden and Jakirovic first met face-to-face in a heated touchline clash in the Turkish Super Lig during early 2025, while Holden was working at Adana Demirspor and Jakirovic was managing Kayserispor.



He said: “Sergei’s assistant recognised me during the Hull interview and I got the job. They appreciated I took over an already-relegated side and wanted someone who knew the Championship.

“Maybe squaring up to an opposition manager is the secret to success and hope he might give you a job in the future! It went in my favour in the end and the rest is history.

With promotion secured, Hull are finally free of EFL transfer restrictions ahead of the 2026–27 season.

The club had been serving a two-window fee limitation—reduced from three on appeal—over late payments to rival clubs.



Holden added: “We need to look at the bigger picture. The United game is the first game of the season, and it is not going to dictate our whole season.

“Sergej and his team deserve so much credit. To turn up in English football unannounced and to get promoted with a transfer embargo, is one of the most magical things that’s happened in the Championship in the last 20 years.”

The camaraderie between the two is obvious when Sergej wanders into the room mid-interview, cheekily trying to negotiate a guest appearance on Holden’s family YouTube channel, Holden It Together.

The YouTube show will cover Hull’s first season in the top-flight since 2017 and offers an insight into grief.

Holden and TV presenter wife Danielle tragically lost their daughter Cici, aged 17 months, after she contracted meningococcal septicaemia, while they were on holiday in Lanzarote in May 2012.



The family hopes their channel serves as a beacon for others facing loss—proof that even in the darkest moments, couples and families can work through grief together.

Holden explained: “When Cici passed we were on the canvas for a long time. We miss her every day.

“Now we hope that if you watch us in action at home in our real life, it’s a tale of hope and inspiration, showing how we can come through something so tragic and devastating.

“We’re trying to shine a light on just a real honest family who are trying to have a little bit of fun and not take life too seriously.

“It sounds a bit cliche, but if it can help one person, because there will be someone sat at home and struggling who maybe reads or listens to this and thinks, bloody hell, he’s in a tough industry himself, but he’s still prepared to talk.



“And I say to people all the time, ‘give me a shout on Instagram or anything’, I’m always up for talking about stuff like this.

“I’ll be honest, it helps me selfishly because I’m able to talk about Cici, it’s been a long time that we’ve not been with her and we miss her.”

The couple’s children Joey, Ellis, Mitzi and Chase, who wants to be a YouTuber, are all characters on the fun channel.

Joey and Ellis joined Holden on ‘lads’ holiday in Ibiza this summer, with Steven Gerrard and his wife Alex sorting them out a VIP table at Ocean Beach when it was sold out. Danielle flew out for the day.

Holden was hired as Gerrard’s assistant at Saudi Pro League club Al-Ettifaq in 2024 after delivering a “stinging attack” in his interview.



The current Hull coach replaced Ian Parker on the Anfield hero’s staff after impressing during an interview at London airport hotel.

Holden said: “He almost sees the game in slow motion. He is one of the greatest players this country has ever produced.

“Whether you are a United fan or not. He is one of the greatest. I got to spend that time inside his head. He’s incredible at handling pressure and his work ethic is second to none.”

Gerrard invited Holden to do a presentation as part of his interview process in early 2024, asking him to analyse a poor performance from Al-Ettifaq.

Holden said: “I just thought I’ll be honest with him, he comes from where I come from, he’s worked his way up from humble beginnings to megastardom.

“It was a tough process but I delivered a stinging attack on his team’s performance and he appreciated my honesty and my take on football.”

Holden himself has dreams head coach return one day after stints with Oldham, Bristol City, Stoke City and Charlton. But first it is all steam ahead with Hull’s Prem season.

Sports.title: FPL tips: The five biggest mistakes to avoid in Gameweek 1
Sports.content:
If you make a bad start in FPL it’s a tough task to recover. So, get your team off to a winning season by avoiding these five big mistakes, provided by our friends at Fantasy Football Hub.

1 - Picking non-starters

There’s nothing worse than picking a player in your FPL squad who doesn’t even start in Gameweek 1 and there’s definitely some popular picks who could fall into that category this season.

Spurs goalkeeper Martin Dubravka (£4.0m) has been selected by 22.4% of managers, with many hoping for a starter at the lowest price point in the game. But it’s his team-mate Antonin Kinsky (£4.5m) who will be first choice between the sticks.

You can defend yourself against any blatantly poor picks by getting your latest draft rated for free by AI in seconds over on Fantasy Football Hub. Simply take a screenshot of your team, upload it to the site and the AI will give you a % score out of 100!

‌



View 4 Images Get your latest draft rated for free by AI in seconds (Image: Fantasy Football Hub)

2 - Falling for pre-season form

It’s easy to be lured in by pre-season form, with plenty of fantasy managers still carrying the scars from backing Chelsea’s Christopher Nkunku in 2024/25, whose hot streak in the summer failed to translate into actual fantasy points come August.

This pre-season has been more truncated than ever given that some sides were already back in training in early July when some of their squad were still in the US at the World Cup. For example, Manchester City were still welcoming players back with less than 10 days to their opening fixture.

Jamie Gittens (£6.0m) has two goals and two assists for Chelsea in pre-season, but didn’t make the starting line-up for their final pre-season friendly, while Crystal Palace’s top performers Matheus Franca (£5.0m) and Eddie Nkteitah (£5.5m) were only substitutes in their final friendly, with three goals apiece.

‌



3 - Backing the unknowns

This season it feels like there’s more uncertainty than ever, with plenty of managerial changes across the Premier League, some teams in Europe for the first time and some disruption to pre-season caused by a World Cup hangover.

It’s important to try to avoid as much of that uncertainty as possible in your FPL teams by selecting nailed starters in settled squads. Actively look to avoid new signings to the Premier League and players from the promoted sides in your Gameweek 1 starting line-up.

Try to avoid players who are heavily speculated of moves in the transfer window, like Everton’s Iliman Ndiaye (£6.0m). Then there’s players like Arsenal’s Christian Mosquera (£5.5m) who could be quickly displaced if the Gunners sign another centre-back before Tuesday September 1.

4 - Having no plan

To fail to plan is to plan to fail. The worst thing to do at the start of the season is failing to think ahead. As a starting point, look at the fixtures for the opening five gameweeks which comes before a long international break. Also ensure you have cover on your bench, in case injuries or suspensions hit early.

‌



View 4 Images Look at the fixtures for the opening five gameweeks (Image: Fantasy Football Hub)

Within the FPL community, there’s momentum gathering for playing the Bench Boost chip early in one of the opening two gameweeks, with cheaper picks from Ipswich Town in Gameweek 1 for the visit of Sunderland, or from Coventry City in Gameweek 2 against Hull.

Don’t go too much the other way and book in transfers either, since the start of the season is the most unpredictable, especially with the transfer window still open. Also have a look at how your team might shape up from one gameweek to the next.

5 - Being too different

Picking a low owned fantasy asset for Gameweek 1 that nobody is talking about that goes on to score a double digit haul is the ultimate fantasy flex. There’s early bragging rights as you take an early lead in those mini leagues against your mates.

‌



However, with over 500 players to choose from, and perhaps only a few diamonds in the rough, it is very easy to get it wrong with a differential pick and end up playing catch up early doors. Taking those risky chances with captaincy is even more extreme.

FPL managers sometimes fear the highly owned picks and the boring play. But it is important to remember that the template picks have earned that status for a reason. They have the most potential for fantasy points, it’s as simple as that.

Sports.title: Premier League introduce nine new rules for 2026/27 season including more VAR
Sports.content:
Premier League introduce nine new rules for 2026/27 season including more VAR

There are a host of new rules for players, managers and fans to get their heads around ahead of the new season

View 3 Images VAR will have a greater say in decisions this season (Image: John Walton/PA Wire)

The new Premier League season will see the introduction of nine new rules aimed at improving the spectacle. Many of the guidelines aim to reduce time-wasting, while some will see an increased use of technology.

‌



Many were successfully deployed at the World Cup, which saw a marked increase in the time the ball was in play. At the tournament in North America, the ball was in play for just over an hour on average, compared to just under 57 minutes at Qatar 2022.

‌



While many of the new rules will be welcomed, some may be met with trepidation as they will mean an increased use of VAR, which remains a source of frustration for many fans.

‌



Ahead of the 2026/27 season opener between champions Arsenal and newly-promoted Coventry City, here's a round-up of the new regulations.

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

Throw-ins: Throws not taken within five seconds will be awarded to the other side. However, that won't apply to long throws which are regarded as set-piece routines.

‌



Sky and TNT Sports to broadcast player-ref audio during Premier League games READ MORE :

Mikel Arteta 'fighting' to change Premier League rule that would suit Arsenal READ MORE :

Goal-kicks: Keepers have also been given a five-second limit. If the kick isn't taken within that time, the referee will have the power to award a corner to the attacking side.

Players going down: If a player randomly drops to the ground, stopping play, they must leave the pitch even if they are not seen by a physio. However, the rule will not be enforced if the player has been fouled and the offending player has been carded.

Substitutions: Substituted players can no longer trudge off the pitch at a snail's pace. Now, they must get off within 10 seconds. If they don't, the player replacing them will have to wait a minute before entering the fray.

‌



View 3 Images Substituted players will have long to get off the pitch (Image: PA)

Goalkeeper timeout: The sight of keepers randomly hitting the deck to burn up seconds has also been combatted. Now, if a keeper is seen by a physio, the manager will have 10 seconds to nominate a player to go off for a minute. If he doesn't decide within 10 seconds, the caption will automatically go off for 60 seconds. The rule won't be enforced if the keeper has been fouled or is bleeding.

Handball from a goal-kick: The rules around handball during a goal-kick routine have been tidied up. Now, any kick of the ball during a goal-kick will be regarded as the kick being taken. Therefore, should any player touch the ball, a penalty will automatically be awarded.

‌



View 3 Images There will be greater scrutiny on set-pieces this season (Image: Getty Images)

Second yellow cards: As we saw at the World Cup, VAR can now be deployed to assess second yellow cards that have been awarded. However, the technology won't be used for potential second bookings that haven't been shown.

Set-piece goals: VAR will also be used to review whether a foul has been committed before the set-piece was taken. If a foul is spotted, the goal will be ruled out and the set-piece retaken.

Article continues below

Mistaken identity: VAR can now intervene to ensure the right player is punished for an offence. It won't be applied as it was at the World Cup, where Paraguay's Miguel Almiron was punished for a dive after the USA was initially booked for a foul. In the Premier League, it must be for the same offence, potentially in the case of a mix-up amid a crowded box.

Arsenal are racing to complete their remaining business before the transfer window slams shut on September 1. After a slow start to the summer window, the Premier League champions’ patience has been rewarded as they have since managed to add crucial depth ahead of their title defence.

‌



The Gunners will go into Friday’s Premier League season opener against Coventry City buoyed by their recent 3-0 drubbing of rivals Manchester City in the Community Shield. New arrivals Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis are expected to play a pivotal role as Mikel Arteta looks to compete across four competitions again.

And Arsenal are not slowing down just yet, with their sporting director Andrea Berta closing in on a deal to bring in versatile defender Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. In terms of potential outgoing players, Gabriel Jesus, Gabriel Martinelli and Fabio Vieira have been listed for sale.

Ethan Nwaneri transfer stance

Arsenal have decided to prioritise loan offers for Nwaneri ahead of the summer transfer deadline, according to a report. The 19-year-old's future has been the subject of much speculation this summer due to concerns surrounding his lack of game time under Arteta.

‌



He was claimed by Fabrizio Romano to be on his way out of the door after being left out of Arsenal’s Community Shield squad which beat City. The likes of Galatasaray, AC Milan and other Premier League clubs were said to be interested.

Sports.title: Richard Masters delivers fresh Man City statement after Arsenal chief requests clarity
Sports.content:
Richard Masters delivers fresh Man City statement after Arsenal chief requests clarity

Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick claims everyone in the Premier League deserves clarity on Manchester City's alleged 115 breaches of financial rules with the independent commission still yet to reach a verdict

View 2 Images Richard Masters is confident the investigation into Man City's alleged financial breaches will be concluded organically (Image: Getty Images)

Premier League Chief Executive Richard Masters insists the independent commission investigating Manchester City's alleged 115 breaches of financial rules "need time and space to do their work" - even if the process is taking "longer than expected."

‌



On the eve of the new season, the Premier League is facing increased pressure to resolve the "hugely complex" case once and for all, three-and-a-half years after City were originally charged.

‌



Arsenal chief executive Richard Garlick is the latest figure calling for clarity, over 18 months after the disciplinary hearing was concluded. City have always denied all charges and any wrongdoing.

‌



CEO Masters said when asked if the investigation is in danger of being forgotten: "It will resolve itself, but as you know, I literally can't say anything about it.

Pro Ref implement Premier League crackdown on grappling as Howard Webb fires warning READ MORE :

World Cup red card 'troubled' Howard Webb as conspiracy theorists slammed READ MORE :

"There's only one available option, which is to allow the process to reach its natural conclusion and I can't talk about the substance of the case, I can't talk about the timing of the case.

"Our rules are very clear about that. Yesterday, I accepted that it would take longer than perhaps anyone had expected.

‌



"The knowledge that people wanted to know - what the outcome was - needed to know what the outcome was. But the process was the process. I literally can't answer beyond what I've already said."

When pushed on whether there is anything the Premier League could have done to speed things up, Masters added: "We've always said that the commission needs time and space to do their work, and in the end, as you know, it's the league's job as the regulator to provide the evidences there, to put serious allegations in front of the independent commission, the independent process, to establish the truth."

View 2 Images Richard Masters was speaking ahead of the new Premier League season which kicks off on Friday (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Masters was then asked whether he understands the level of frustration at the continued delay, to which he responded: "I just have to accept the fact that people are frustrated and want to know and I can't add anything further."

Some executives at top-flight clubs are frustrated that the process has been so drawn-out, particularly after Everton were ordered to pay Burnley £35million in June due to the impact of a breach of the Premier League's financial rules.

The 59-year-old isn't feeling direct heat from other clubs though, stating: “I obviously speak to clubs all the time. It’s not necessarily a topic of conversation that is top of the list.

‌



“[There are] lots of other things to talk about and do. As you say, the Premier League moves on. It’s starting [again] on Friday evening.”

Gunners chief Garlick told the BBC: "It has gone on for a while. Everybody - the league and the teams - would want the clarity around what's going to happen next.

"But it's not something that I can control. It's not something that I can speculate on. And I just hope that there is a solution very quickly."

Sports.title: How does Arteta deliver step five of his Arsenal plan?
Sports.content:
When Mikel Arteta arrived at Arsenal, he presented a five-step plan to go from crisis club to glory. Welcome to step five: create a dynasty.

Up until this year, steps one to four were about getting Arsenal back to the Arsene Wenger days of winning major honours again.

With his Arsenal team reigning Premier League champions again, Arteta is now striving to do something the great Wenger never could.

No Arsenal team has successfully defended a top-flight title since the Gunners won three leagues in a row ending in 1935. Not even Wenger's double-winning or 'Invincibles' teams backed up their historic achievement with an immediate title win the following year.

In his pre-match messages, Arteta often turns to creating history as a huge motivation for his team and there will be no doubt he will push the 'back-to-back' narrative to his Arsenal squad over the next nine months.

But dynasty and history are not the only goals Arsenal are aiming for this season. Despite being champions of England - and many analysts' pick to go and win again - there is still improvement needed from the last campaign.

Arsenal

Coventry City Friday 21st August 6:30pm Kick off 8:00pm

Arsenal have enjoyed a memorable last year but more efficiency in attack could have made last term a superb campaign.

The euphoric scenes of last season - which included countless parties outside the Emirates Stadium and across the world - masked over the Champions League final defeat, where Arsenal failed to get a shot on target for the 114 minutes after they took the lead against Paris Saint-Germain.

It was a missed opportunity for Arteta's side to write themselves into more history - and showed that for all their defensive excellence, there was still a sense of predictability about them going forwards, with question marks over how much they could create and score from open play.

It was not just in the Champions League final where Arsenal struggled in this department. It was the story of their season. While Arsenal were outstanding in the defence and set-pieces category, their open-play numbers left much to be desired.

Image: Arsenal were outside the top three teams in the league last season for open play metrics

For all of Arsenal's success last term, they were not in the top three teams in the Premier League for key attacking metrics from open play. The numbers weren't bad, but it is a clear area of improvement.

The question is whether they can rectify that - and become more unpredictable - this season. The 3-0 win over Manchester City in the Community Shield, where Arsenal dominated the game, scored three times from open play, and did not create a single set-piece chance, was an early sign of progress.

Yet the summer transfer window has raised some doubts about whether that attacking efficiency will come and where it will come from, especially regarding the forward line.

Morgan Rogers was deemed the No 1 attacking target before Chelsea stumped up £117m to bring him from Aston Villa. Then came the Vinicius Junior pursuit, an exciting saga at first - but his re-commitment to Real Madrid ended that dream and sent Arsenal back to the drawing board.

Christos Tzolis arrived early in the window as the first outfield signing but was brought in as a direct - and younger - replacement for Leandro Trossard. Other than that, Arsenal go into the season with the same attacking players who ended last season.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Sam Blitz explains why Arsenal's emphatic win over Manchester City has led to plenty of transfer debates for the Gunners

Arsenal still have time to rectify this in the window - and last season's late pursuit of Eberechi Eze showed players can arrive late and produce big title-winning moments in the season.

But with Aston Villa and Chelsea waiting in a tricky opening three games this time around, Arsenal will be put under the microscope early on.

Why Arsenal's solution could come away from transfers

This summer, Arteta has pointed out that transfers are not the only solution to the issues Arsenal still need to address.

"We will go from strength to strength," he said during pre-season. "Whether it's the players we have, to take them to a different level, or with the market that is still open to recruit as well. We're optimistic about it."

Arsenal have room to grow this season - but the players who were there last term can contribute more, just as much as new signings could. Last summer's midfield and attacking signings - Martin Zubimendi, Noni Madueke, Viktor Gyokeres and Eze - all had good seasons, but not great ones.

So much so that none of the above quartet started Arsenal's Champions League final in Budapest, as Arteta went for the more familiar options who he had known for longer. If any of those forward players improve on last season's campaigns, then Arsenal are capable of finding another level in attack.

It is not just a goalscoring conundrum, but a chance creation one too. Chief creator Martin Odegaard limited to just 14 league starts. He still averaged the third-highest chance creation record per 90 in the Premier League last season.

Had the Arsenal captain played more minutes, their attacking output would have increased. Odegaard was Arsenal's best player in the statement Community Shield win over City, so if the Norwegian is able to build on a solid World Cup and start the season strongly, it's almost as helpful as a new signing.

Image: Martin Odegaard was Arsenal's best player in the Community Shield win over Man City

"I'm sure this year if we can maintain him fit, available with the players around him, we're going to see a very different Martin," said Arteta after the win over City.

"And I sense from the first day that he joined that he has something else in the belly that he wants to prove and show it, because the team needs it as well."

Another creativity boost for Arsenal is Bruno Guimaraes - who arrives from Newcastle as the club's second-most expensive signing.

The Brazilian is a defensive boost given his tough-tackling nature, but last season Guimaraes was in the top 10 players for breaking the opposition back line through passing the ball.

You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enable Datawrapper cookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the This content is provided by, which may be using cookies and other technologies. To show you this content, we need your permission to use cookies. You can use the buttons below to amend your preferences to enablecookies or to allow those cookies just once. You can change your settings at any time via the Privacy Options Unfortunately we have been unable to verify if you have consented to Datawrapper cookies. To view this content you can use the button below to allow Datawrapper cookies for this session only. Enable Cookies Allow Cookies Once

Note how former No 1 target Rogers also ranked highly in this discipline - highlighting a certain profile Arteta was looking for in the transfer window.

"He's a player which obviously has tremendous timing and intuition to win the ball back and progress play very fast," Arteta said about Guimaraes after he joined.

"He's a player that is very comfortable putting people through, moving between the lines, moving in behind.

"And then he's a goal threat. He's got a smell and a really good timing to get in the box. And he has the capacity to finish the actions."

Arsenal were not able to produce a player who could produce these moments to open up defences as regularly as Guimaraes last season. But if the Brazilian plays regularly alongside Odegaard this season, then Arsenal may have a better attack than most people think.

And this week, there was a a hint from Arteta that he wants to see a different type of Arsenal this season. When asked about him being a "defending" Premier League champion, he corrected that statement by saying he and his team are "attacking" another Premier League title.

Are we set to see a more expansive Arsenal this season - led by the likes of a resurgent Odegaard and new signings such as Guimaraes and Tzolis? They may actually have to be more adventurous going forward if they are to retain their crown.

Amid all the transfer talk, one factor that has gone slightly under the radar is William Saliba's extended absence with a back injury. A key cog from Arsenal's irresistible defence is missing for the early part of the season.

Image: Arsenal's win rate drops from 68 per cent to 50 per cent without William Saliba starting

Saliba is so often branded a 'Rolls Royce' - or a 'cheat code' - of a defender, mainly due to his pace to stop counter-attacks and transitions. No other member of the Arsenal team has delivered that skill so consistently at the highest level.

Arsenal still have Gabriel, one of the league's outstanding defensive players. But with Jurrien Timber also playing fitness catch-up and Ben White's injury record, Arsenal enter the season with a less experienced defence than usual. Even with the imminent arrival of Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa, they may not be able to rely so heavily on their defensive superiority at the start of this season.

For all those concerns, Arsenal would do well to remember they come into the new campaign as the reigning champions of England. On top of that, they did not lose a single match in 90 minutes during the Champions League last season.

They were already a very good football team before the summer and have added some quality to it, albeit not as much as they would have liked so far.

Arsenal are also the sole member of the so-called 'Big Six' who are not going through a managerial or squad-building rebuild - and are attacking this season from a higher platform of success.

As a result, the message from Arteta and Arsenal this summer has surrounded evolution, rather than revolution. And this Arsenal team now takes on a different climate.

The past few years have been about this team getting over the line, but what will we see from champions Arsenal this season?

Sports.title: Key questions and predictions as F1 returns
Sports.content:
Formula 1's summer break is over and the 2026 season restarts in the Netherlands this weekend as the championship run-in looms over the final months of the campaign.

We asked Sky Sports F1 pundit Karun Chandhok to run the rule over some of the key questions left to be answered on and off track this year and predict how things might pan out from here…

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See what some of the Formula 1 drivers, including Lewis Hamilton, George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, got up to during the summer break!

How many drivers still have a realistic title shot?

Kimi Antonelli's 50-point championship lead puts him firmly in the hunt, but fewer points cover Lewis Hamilton in second down to Lando Norris, the winner of the last race in Hungary, in fifth. With two Sprints and up to 12 Grands Prix to go, there are potentially as many as 316 points left to play for between now and December.

Karun says: "I think, realistically, this is Antonelli's championship to lose. Nobody has come back from this big a points deficit since we went to this scoring system in 2010. Kimi is driving well, he has got a lot of confidence in the car and the way it's working for him.

"The only Achilles' heel seems to be Mercedes' reliability. That could be a challenge, but they are going to keep improving that. So realistically, I think it is his championship to lose, which is an extraordinary achievement in just his second year in F1.

"The only thing I would say is, with the way the upgrades and updates are going, it will be interesting to see what Ferrari can do, and also whether any of Mercedes' upgrades help George Russell out, because it does feel like he has had obviously more bad luck but also a pace disadvantage this year.

"I think it is only Lewis or maybe George who could challenge him, but it's more his to lose."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the Formula 1 season set to resume after the summer break, we look back at how Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has built a 50-point lead in the driver standings.

Which team is the one to watch for development?

In-season car development is always crucial in Formula 1 but the stakes have been raised this year with teams still in the early stages of understanding how to unlock the best performance from the all-new 2026 aerodynamic rules and engines. The first half of the season saw teams make big jumps in performance at races they brought update packages, and others did not, with that trend expected to continue after the summer break.

Karun says: "I'm interested to see what McLaren do. Clearly the car was very good in Budapest and that bodes well for the Dutch Grand Prix because whoever is good in Budapest should have a good car for Zandvoort.

"And they've got more bits coming this weekend on the rear end of the car as well, which is the second half of the update.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Watch the moment that Lando Norris claims victory at the Hungarian Grand Prix!

"The big one to keep an eye out for is Red Bull, because they have been a bit more inconsistent and there's a bit of a battle on for them to play catch-up.

"If you look at it across the season, they have had the fourth-fastest car, which is not ideal in terms of trying to keep Max happy and at the team.

"So, Red Bull are the ones I'm most interested in watching out for to see if they can dig themselves out of this hole in terms of inconsistencies."

Where will Max Verstappen end up driving for 2027?

The big question on which the volatility of the driver market hinges. Max Verstappen is contracted to Red Bull until the end of 2028 but a position outside the top two of the Drivers' Championship at the summer break - he sits in sixth place - means he is free to activate a break clause in the deal for the end of this year, should he wish. The answer to the question of whether he will or not remains unknown with Verstappen thought to have until October to tell Red Bull should he want to leave. Immediate alternative options for him for 2027, however, should he want to continue in F1 remain uncertain despite links to McLaren and Mercedes.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Relive Max Verstappen's troublesome 2026 season, with the Red Bull driver having suffered multiple issues.

Karun says: "I have no idea when Max will end up driving in 2027 but I think realistically, I don't think he knows yet either.

"I think he is waiting to see where the Red Bull goes and really what other options there are."

Will Fernando Alonso race on or retire from F1 for 2027?

Fernando Alonso said he would use the summer break to decide on whether he will extend his F1 career into a record-extending 24th campaign next season. The Spaniard, who turned 45 in July and became a father for the first time earlier this year, has downplayed suggestions his decision completely rests on how competitive he expects Aston Martin to be in 2027, saying that it will also be influenced on how he feels about the sport's current rules.

Karun says: "I think if Aston can demonstrate that they are going to make progress and Honda can demonstrate that they are making progress and they can give Alonso a car that at least gets him into Q3 and gives him something to fight for in 2027, then he will stick around.

"He is not going to stick around to be someone who gets knocked out in Q1 all the time."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Fernando Alonso said Aston Martin’s new upgrades delivered improvements in Hungary.

How high will Aston Martin get up the grid?

The clear underperformer of the season's first half after all manner of issues with their 2026 chassis and Honda engine left them at the back of the grid, Aston Martin delivered what they hope will provide the first of many steps forward with their first car upgrade last time out in Hungary. Further revisions to Adrian Newey's AMR26 and the first long-awaited engine upgrade, which is set to arrive at Zandvoort, offer the potential for further progress heading towards 2027.

Karun says: "Aston Martin have got to get themselves in a position where they need to end this year at least occasionally getting into Q3 because that then lays the foundation for 2027 and beyond.

"The engine upgrades will be critical for that. If you look at their straight-line speed at Spa, it was shocking. They brought the updated chassis to Budapest and that seemed to give them some performance advantage, a decent step.

"So really with the engine advantage, they might occasionally sneak themselves into Q3, which would be good progress but more importantly, a good foundation."

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player With the last Formula One race coming up at Zandvoort, look back at some of the most dramatic moments throughout the years at the Dutch Grand Prix.

How many drivers will win races over the remaining rounds?

F1 broke for summer on a run of five different winners in as many races with both Mercedes drivers, both Ferrari drivers and McLaren's Lando Norris standing on the top step of the podium during that run.

Karun says: "I think there is a chance we could see both Ferrari drivers, McLaren drivers and Mercedes drivers winning races, and Max.

"If Red Bull do upgrade well and bring good bits and pieces, then we could see Max winning. He wasn't that far off in Austria, and the car steadily made progress. They need a couple of jumps and they could do it."

What will Sepang be like on F1's return and who might the track favour?

For the first time in nine years, F1 will race at the much-loved Sepang International Circuit in October after Malaysia agreed to host the Bahrain Grand Prix. Sepang built a reputation as both a driver and fan favourite across its 18 years on the calendar, with the track featuring challenging corner combinations and providing good racing.

Karun says: "I love Sepang. I first raced there in 2001, which was my first year of international racing. I've been back in lots of different categories and have always absolutely loved the circuit.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Formula 1 has added Malaysia to its 2026 schedule to host the Bahrain Grand Prix that was postponed earlier in the season.

"I think it is a really interesting, challenging layout, good for racing. I'm delighted to see everyone going back there, albeit temporarily.

"I think we are going to see a fantastic race. For this year's cars, there are plenty of opportunities to harvest and recharge the batteries and energy around chunks of the lap, so it should be a pretty good race all round.

"It is going to be hot, so anyone who can keep the tyre temperatures under control will be in good shape."

Who will win the 2026 championships?

Antonelli's half-century lead at mid-season makes him the clear bookmakers' favourite ahead of Lewis Hamilton and George Russell, who was most people's tips for the title at the start of the year.

Mercedes would likely have been away and clear already and not just 72 points ahead of Ferrari had they not suffered from reliability problems. Nonetheless, Ferrari outscored them in each of the three races before the summer break and, with reliability on their side, aren't to be ruled out yet. McLaren were 78 points back on Red Bull with 12 races to go in 2024 and ended up as champions.

Karun says: "I think this is Antonelli's drivers' title to lose, and Mercedes' Constructors' Championship to lose."

Sports.title: England skittle Pakistan at Headingley on Root's return as Test captain
Sports.content:
Joe Root's second spell as England Test captain began with his side skittling Pakistan for 171 at Headingley as Ollie Robinson and Josh Tongue each bagged five-wicket hauls around a lengthy rain delay and a brief fightback from the tourists.

Root is back in charge following Ben Stokes' shock international retirement in June and charged with turning around the team's fortunes after seven defeats and just one win in their last 10 games, across fixtures against India, Australia and New Zealand.

Bar wet weather preventing any play from 11.50pm-1.45pm, and Abdullah Shafique (61) and Imam-ul-Haq (42) putting on a stand of 91 from 6-2, this was an excellent day for Root, with Pakistan rolled in 48.1 overs before the hosts closed on 112-2 in reply, trailing by 59.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ollie Robinson's fifth Test five-for included a beauty to bowl Pakistan's top-scorer Abdullah Shafique for 61

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Josh Tongue completed his five-for and ended the Pakistan innings in one foul swoop by bowling Mohammad Abbas

Score summary - England vs Pakistan, first Test, Headingley Pakistan 171 all out in 48.1 overs in first innings (put in to bat): Abdullah Shafique (61), Imam-ul-Haq (42); Salman Ali Agha (21); Josh Tongue (5-46), Ollie Robinson (5-51) England 112-2 after 25 overs in first innings (trail by 59 runs): Joe Root (37no), Emilio Gay (33), Jordan Cox (23no), Ben Duckett (15); Mohammad Abbas (1-34), Mohammad Ali (1-38)

England lost Ben Duckett (15) lbw and Emilio Gay (33) caught at slip, to Mohammad Abbas and Mohammad Ali respectively, leaving Jordan Cox (23no) - into the side at No 3 in place of the injured Jacob Bethell - and Root (37no) to usher the side to the 7.30pm stumps with an unbroken stand of 64.

The day had been extended after the earlier rain, which could return in droves on day two.

Root - whose first stint in charge from 2017-2022 preceded the fabulously entertaining but ultimately flawed Bazball era - had no hesitation in bowling after winning the toss under leaden skies on his home ground and that decision reaped immediate rewards.

Robinson (5-51) inflicted a platinum duck on Azan Awais, trapping the opener lbw from around the wicket as a wicket fell to the first ball of a Test match in England for the first time in 19 years, and then pinned Shan Masood (5) leg before from over the wicket.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Robinson trapped Azan Awais lbw for a duck from the first ball of the Headingley Test

Pakistan battled to 23-2 from 9.4 overs before the rain arrived, during which time England burned two reviews looking for further breakthroughs, and then progressed to 97-3 once play resumed, only for Tongue (5-46) nicking off Imam to trigger a collapse.

The away side lost their final eight wickets for 74 and last five for 21, with the clatter including Robinson bowling Shafique with a beauty that jagged in prodigiously and the same bowler pinning Saud Shakeel (5) lbw after the batter took two long to request a review that would have saved him - the ball was set to soar over leg stump.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Pakistan's Saud Shakeel was left to rue taking too long to review an lbw dismissal - with Robinson's delivery set to bounce over the stumps

Tongue's hat-trick hopes dashed as Pakistan razed

Tongue was on a hat-trick as the players emerged after tea having bowled stand-in Pakistan captain Salman Ali Agha (21) - who is deputising for Babar Azam (hand) - through the gate and then trapped Ali Usman (0) lbw before the break.

Pakistan No 9 Khurram Shahzad (14) denied Tongue that magic moment, with a crunching cover-driven four, but Tongue snared a fourth Test five-for by going on to remove Mohammad Rizwan (12) lbw and obliterate the off stump of Abbas (2).

Robinson's fifth five-for in the format, and second of the summer, could have come two balls earlier than it did, only for Gus Atkinson to spill Khurram's hack to mid-on, yet Atkinson made no mistake shortly after when Khurram sliced down the ground once again.

This is the skilful Robinson's first Test since the series opener against New Zealand at Lord's, a game in which he bagged a triple-wicket maiden, seven wickets all told and was named Player of the Match, and he bowled with immense accuracy and control here, too.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Stuart Broad looks at why Robinson has previously been over-looked for England selection and what his key assets are

The same could not be said of Jofra Archer (0-26 from nine overs), who struggled with his line and length at times - conceding 12 runs off his fourth over - and looked very much like a man who has had a diet of white-ball cricket over the last few months.

Archer, who was hooked after two overs after sharing the new ball with Robinson, should be better for the runout.

Shafique had entered this Test off the back of a fifty in the sole warm-up against a County Select XI last week and an unbeaten 160 in the Test win in the West Indies earlier this month.

He looked well attuned to red-ball cricket - once he had survived a one-sided early tussle with Tongue, that is - as he compiled a sixth Test fifty, from 82 deliveries, before falling to Robinson's jaffa.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Ben Duckett and Emilio Gay were dismissed in quick succession during the first day of the first Test against Pakistan

England opener Gay had bagged a pair playing for the County XI against Pakistan in that aforementioned tune-up fixture in Beckenham but he got off the mark second ball in Leeds with a nerve-settling single and then stroked and clipped a number of pleasing boundaries before prodding to slip.

The home side could face a long wait before they bat again as Thursday's forecast is rotten but whenever play does resume, it will do so with England in a strong position, with Abbas' fellow Pakistan seamers Khurram and Ali unable to match his precision as they leaked runs and Root now ominously settled.

Tongue: England in a great position

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player England's Josh Tongue reflects on a positive first day of the Test match against Pakistan

England fast bowler Josh Tongue (5-46), talking to Sky Sports:

"We're in a great position now but that first hour tomorrow morning - it might do a bit more at 11am.

"If we focus on that first hour, we can get a good lead.

"As a bowling unit, we were very good and Robinson was excellent. It was similar to his performance at Lord's against New Zealand.

"He's an exceptional bowler when he hits his lines and lengths and he showed that today."
