View image in fullscreen Benjamin Nygren puts Celtic ahead in their Champions League playoff against Lask. Photograph: Stuart Wallace/Shutterstock

Lask had a headed goal chalked off for offside before Durán struck his first and Sinisalo made another couple of saves before the break.

The Celtic captain, Callum McGregor, fired a deflected 20-yard shot off the inside of a post as chances kept coming in the second half, and Usor squandered two excellent opportunities.

Reo Hatate came on to huge acclaim in what could be one of his final Celtic Park appearances before Durán came close twice from long range before his second goal of the night.

The goal hero got another massive cheer for sprinting back to his own byline to make a challenge and Sinisalo continued to look assured as Celtic maintained their clean sheet.

Sports.title: ‘Believe your eyes’: Masters says Premier League’s integrity cannot be doubted
Sports.content:
Richard Masters has sought to reassure fans that the Premier League remains “everything that it should be” after the Folarin Balogun red-card scandal called the integrity of disciplinary decisions into question.

Both Masters, the chief executive of the Premier League, and Howard Webb, the chief refereeing officer for English football, were critical of the process that led to Fifa’s ­disciplinary committee suspending the USA striker’s one-game ban for a year after an intervention by the US president, Donald Trump. Masters went further, calling for a candidate with “a different offer” to run against Gianni Infantino for Fifa president next year.

Asked about the Balogun affair, Masters – who was speaking in advance of the new Premier League season beginning on Friday – said: “We should be talking about looking back on the World Cup and the football that was played, and Spain being obviously the best team and ­England’s agonising semi-final defeat,” Masters said. “We’re not. We’re talking about other issues. I think that’s a huge shame. The Balogun issue … is very difficult to comprehend, really, when you look at it.”

Masters insisted that the taint of the scandal would not reach out into the Premier League, even as refereeing conspiracy theories continue among fans. “Do people believe their eyes? I do scroll through social media every now and then. I do bump into some of the stuff that people are saying and thinking out there,” Masters said. “But I do still believe that fans, when they turn up to matches that are 99% sold out, when they watch what’s going on on the pitch, they see everything that it should be. It’s still the same.

“It’s English football. Everyone’s trying their best. Referees are trying their best. There’s lots of controversy, but it is what it says it is.”

The Premier League, as a member of the World Leagues Association, is still waiting for the outcome of a complaint made against Fifa to the European Commission two years ago over a lack of consultation over the fixture calendar.

Masters said it was vital that Infantino was properly challenged in the Fifa presidential election next year. “I think that what needs to happen now is another candidate needs to emerge within the deadline with a new offer, a different offer, that can hopefully unify the confederations,” he said.

Webb said he had been “really troubled” by the Balogun scandal, as he announced new measures to increase transparency over refereeing decisions in England. “What do we know? We know for sure that a red card was shown. I understand why it was given,” he said.

View image in fullscreen Howard Webb said the game had changed since he was a referee. Photograph: Zac Goodwin/PA

“We know that there was pressure placed by a politician on to Fifa, because that was admitted. And we know that the suspension was taken away for that particular tournament and suspended through a process which seemingly didn’t exist before the tournament started.”

He continued: “We live in a world now which is different to the one that I occupied as a referee. Decisions were previously viewed as correct or incorrect, based on your judgment. Far too often now decisions are viewed as correct or corrupt by people who want to type all over social media. They try to draw inferences around decisions that they don’t agree with and what’s the motivation behind that decision. Which is born out of no facts, no evidence.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

This season, English football’s senior refereeing body, now known as Pro Ref, will seek to publish the assessments of an independent key match incident panel which examines all the biggest decisions taken by Premier League referees each week. As reported by the Guardian, Pro Ref will publish some audio of conversations between referees and players during matches and will continue to use X to publish real time information during match days.

New video assistant referee specialists have been recruited at Stockley Park to expand the pool of officials as Pro Ref seeks to cut the length of time around VAR interventions and eliminate incidents where VARs intervene when – according to ProRef – they should not. “I’d rather have missed interventions than over-interventions,” Webb said. “I’d rather VAR not get involved wrongly to rectify something that wasn’t wrong in the first place, because that’s a ­damaging effect on the game.”

In a further attempt to improve the speed of decision-making, the protocol behind semi-automatic offside technology has been streamlined.

Webb said fans and players alike can also expect to see more penalty kicks awarded for holding at set pieces. “More situations will be penalised, not only in August or September, but throughout the season,” Webb said. “[But] I’m not going to commit to say we’re going to go from here to penalising lots of contact. Contact is still part of the game, we still maintain a high threshold, but this time next year, all being well, we’ll be able to reflect on a season where more offences have been penalised.”

Sports.title: Instant classics, odd inspirations and barcodes: 2026-27’s best and worst kits
Sports.content:
The Premier League season kicks off on Friday and league debutants such as Christos Tzolis and Victor Muñoz, along with masses of fans, will be pulling on their teams’ shiny new strips. There were some lovely efforts at the World Cup (not least by the co-hosts the USA), and others more tedious than a 0-0 draw. It’s a mixed bag once again.

Manchester City have gone with an ombre design, which feels – apposite for a gradient fading of colour – exhausted as a look in 2026. In the most surprising but successful collaboration since Olivia Rodrigo and Robert Smith,Sunderland have teamed up with Elvis Presley, or his estate, anyway, for a pink away shirt that nods to the supporters’ longstanding unofficial anthem Can’t Help Falling in Love.

Here’s a selection of the best, worst and most interesting (for reasons good and bad) that sportswear giants – and Oxen Sports – have in store for us this year.

Chelsea

Chelsea’s new home kit may look like the sort of thing a team called London Blue would wear in one of the early editions of Pro Evo, but it is pretty neat. I cannot stress this enough: the lack of a corporate logo will always make a shirt look better (Sunderland fans also got to enjoy this for pre-season, but alas the Black Cats have a sponsor incoming).

The Blues have rolled out a number of stars to preview their 2026-27 look, first among them Madonna, a longtime supporter often spotted at Stamford Bridge, which is why Cole Palmer and João Pedro made a surprise appearance in her recent video. The 90s polo‑shirt collar is a popular aesthetic this season. The home and away kits – in a sleek black – heavily feature Ted Drake’s famous lion emblem.

View image in fullscreen Chelsea’s financial loss is our aesthetic gain with this classy sponsor-less home kit. Photograph: Darren Walsh/CFC/Getty Images

As a side note, Madonna’s twin daughters play for Tottenham, which I mention only because Spurs have, once again, produced the world’s most insufferably dull kit, presumably designed by Kazimir Malevich.

Liverpool

Surely the kit of the season. An entirely unsubtle homage to the 1989-91 home jersey (and as far as sponsors’ logos go, Candy’s was one of the least hideous), the home shirt is a blast of fun at a time when football – Infantino, VAR, you name it – is increasingly dispiriting. Then again, I am not sure even a top this jazzy can offset the hideousness of Jeff Bezos acquiring a stake in the club.

The white away kit is also a handsome affair, proving that white strips do not have to be boring; again, commiserations to Spurs fans. While the home fit is giving disco, the away is a more demure meet-the-parents type, with a preppy v-shaped neck. I do still miss the old YNWA crest, though.

View image in fullscreen Alexander Isak (left) admires Cody Gakpo (right)’s modelling of the instant classic news Liverpool shirt. Photograph: Luke Williams/Shutterstock

Hull

The Hull accent is one of Timothée Chalamet’s favourites and the actor and keen football fan would no doubt be charmed by the promoted side’s new-but-old look. This kit feels like it belongs on a glorious swamp of a pitch in the mid-to-late 20th century, complete with dribbled juice stains from half-time oranges.

The official reference point is the Tigers’ late 70s aesthetic: wide black and amber stripes and a white collar and trim, the shirt features the HCAFC logo for the first time in 47 years, invoking the spirit of Billy Bremner. It is definitely understated, given how many riotous bangers the club has had in the past (see the amazing tiger-striped 1992 shirt, among others).

Away from the MKM Stadium, Hull will turn out in a much more meh monotone kit with amber accents, but still, sterling work in the main from the city’s homegrown sportswear brand, Oxen Sports.

View image in fullscreen Regan Slater cuts a dash in a kit that evokes his more illustrious 1970s midfield predecessor Billy Bremner. Photograph: Tony King/Getty Images

Newcastle

It is extremely low-hanging fruit to compare this shirt to a barcode, but, seriously, look at it. It’s a barcode. It’s also dizzying to the eye. I’m generally a fan of risk-taking kits – bring on the chaos – but this is, well … the PR blurb describes the pattern as “disrupted”.

Given this design belongs only in the vicinity of a self-service checkout, it is truly an unexpected item in the playing area. Then Adidas chucked some pale blue stripes on to the shoulders just in case fans weren’t distressed enough.

The away strip is an improvement; a refined navy, it has a nice alternative badge of the city’s titular castle and a magpie. Newcastle aren’t the only club that have done too much with their home strip: Macron has produced a striking sash design for Crystal Palace, but, in the words of Hannah Gadsby describing the Pride flag: bit busy.

View image in fullscreen Newcastle’s new manager Matthias Jaissle models a home kit that definitely will not reveal the £120 price tag if you scan it. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

Ipswich

Among what is always extremely strong competition, Ipswich secure the trophy for the most eye-rolling kit “inspiration”. The motif on the round-necked, blue home shirt is, according to Umbro’s press release, a tribute to Portman Road’s floodlights. This is not the only floodlight-inspired design; Nike paid homage to VfL Bochum’s floodlights in 2020-21 – but at least their stadium’s massive pylons are a genuine symbol of the city. As it happens, the weaved pattern is lovely, but the diamonds recall those mood-indicating crystals above the heads of characters in The Sims (officially plumbobs) more than the stadium floodlights.

The change kit is cream with thin red and black horizontal stripes and black side panels. Floodlights 100% snubbed.

View image in fullscreen You would need a very bright floodlight to spot the alleged inspiration for Ipswich’s otherwise

nice home kit. Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty Images

Manchester United

I am haunted by the Adidas stripes on the red home shirt being white, while the ones on the white shorts are black. This would be fine, except the designers have made the stripes so thick – they seem to spread larger each season, like a kid who can no longer be arsed to stay colouring inside the lines – that this looks like one half each of two separate kits; it’s 24 hours before laundry day at the Theatre of Dreams.

The shirt itself is beautiful; the perfect shade of red, a retro collar not too dissimilar to Chelsea’s, but the black touches are not strong enough to cohere with the massive oil streaks on the shorts. The away kit, meanwhile, nods to the 80s, in suave cobalt blue with red touches and trefoil logo. A final positive: it looks like just the one kit.

Sports.title: Manchester City target Roma’s Manu Koné as Spurs talk over Savinho and Marmoush deal
Sports.content:
Manchester City have identified Roma’s Manu Koné as a potential target to strengthen further Enzo Maresca’s options in midfield.

While City have already bought Elliot Anderson for £116m and are closing in on the £85m signing of Lille’s Ayyoub Bouaddi, Maresca admires Koné for his dynamic mode of play. He would be expected to cost about £50m.

The 25-year-old impressed for France at the World Cup, playing five of their eight matches. France won all four of the games he started.

If signed, Koné would add elite-level experience to Maresca’s squad, which is now without Rodri after Spain’s World Cup-winning captain was sold to Barcelona for about £65m on Tuesday.

While Anderson was a first-choice alongside Declan Rice for England at the World Cup and made his Premier League debut for Newcastle in 2021, at 18 Bouaddi is still relatively inexperienced.

On Wednesday, another City midfielder departed when Tijjani Reijnders was sold to Al-Qadsiah in a deal worth about £51m after only one season at the club. While the Dutchman operates as a No 8, Nico González, who plays as a defensive midfielder, may also follow before the window closes on 1 September.

City are still expected to make an official bid for Chelsea’s Enzo Fernández, though they are thought to value him less than the west London club’s £120m asking price.

City’s busy summer also includes their continuing talks with Tottenham regarding the sale of Savinho and Omar Marmoush in a double deal worth about £150m. Savinho has previously been linked with Spurs, while Marmoush has now emerged as a target for Roberto De Zerbi.

No agreement has been reached but negotiations are understood to be progressing well for the Brazilian winger and the Egyptian forward, with De Zerbi believing each will add depth to his squad.

Sports.title: Arsenal agree £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Arsenal have agreed a £51m deal to sign Ezri Konsa from Aston Villa. The Premier League champions have been keen to find defensive cover for William Saliba and Jurriën Timber, who are out with injuries. They have tracked Konsa throughout the summer and have made a breakthrough in the negotiations.

Mikel Arteta hopes Konsa, whose Villa contract has two years to run, can help make light of Saliba’s absence in central defence. The timeframe for the Frenchman’s return is unclear but he is not expected to play before mid-October, having sustained a back injuryin France’s World Cup semi-final defeat against Spain.

Konsa’s appeal is bolstered by the fact he can also play at right-back, where Timber is battling to return from a groin injury which has affected him for months.

Konsa starred for England on their run to the World Cup semi-finals. A fixture in Villa’s successful team, the 28-year-old will encounter fierce competition at Arsenal, especially when Saliba is fit. Arteta rates Saliba’s partnership with Gabriel Magalhães as the best in England but he thinks the addition of a player of Konsa’s calibre is a signal of Arsenal’s desire to build on their title success of last season and dominate.

The manager knows that his team played 63 matches in all competitions last season, which included runs to the Champions League and Carabao Cup finals, and he hopes to have a similar number this time out. As such, he believes he will be able to give Konsa the minutes he would expect, particularly when injuries are factored in. Arteta is also determined to have more high-quality options so that he can better rotate. At present, he has eight defenders, including Myles Lewis-Skelly, who can play in midfield.

Konsa joined Villa from Brentford in 2019 and has been central to their rise under Unai Emery. He has made 286 appearances for them and was a part of the team that won the Europa League last season. Arsenal kick off the new season at home to Coventry on Friday night.

Meanwhile, Villa are braced for another bid from Al-Hilal for Ollie Watkins, after rejecting an offer worth almost £40m for the striker. Al-Hilal are pursuing a move for Villa’s all-time Premier League goalscorer, who has reached double figures in the top flight in his six seasons at the club after joining from Brentford.

If Villa sell Watkins, who has two years on his contract, they would seek to replace the 30-year-old England striker and Emery is a big admirer of Nicolas Jackson, but Chelsea’s valuation of £65m is thought to be prohibitive to any deal. There is an acceptance at Villa that any marquee arrival before the close of the window would probably have to follow another major sale, owing to the Premier League’s financial regulations.

Emery has had to significantly reshape his squad this summer after the departures of Morgan Rogers, Youri Tielemans and Lucas Digne, who joined Chelsea, Manchester United and Paris Saint-Germain respectively, with Konsa now also on the move.

Villa have signed Zion Suzuki as a replacement for Emiliano Martínez, whose future remains unclear. Suzuki, a £30m buy from Parma, will be the first Japanese goalkeeper to play in the Premier League.

Villa have completed the £17m signing of Matteo Ruggeri from Atlético Madrid and remain in talks with Bayern Munich over a deal for João Palhinha and West Ham for Aaron Wan-Bissaka. Villa have also signed Johan Manzambi from Freiburg for a club-record £52m and João Gomes from Wolves for £38m. There could be further sales, with Villa hoping to find Martínez a new club.

Villa gave Watkins, together with Konsa, an extended four-week break after the World Cup. Emery said Watkins volunteered to play in last week’s Super Cup against PSG, but the manager advised him to continue to rest.

Sports.title: Sheffield United co-chair could be disqualified after dispute over £35m debt from club purchase
Sports.content:
The Sheffield United co-chair, Steven Rosen, is facing disqualification as a director by the English Football League after the company through which he bought the club two years ago, COH Sports Bidco Limited, was liquidated.

The winding-up order issued by the high court in London is the result of a dispute between United’s owners and their predecessor, Prince Abdullah’s United World, which claims it is owed £35m by Rosen and his business partner Helmy Eltoukhy in unpaid fees resulting from the £110m sale of the Championship club in December 2024.

Abdullah filed the winding-up petition last month after Rosen and Eltoukhy transferred ownership of the club to a new parent company, 1919 Partners LLC, which he alleged was part of an attempt to avoid paying the outstanding debt.

1919 Partners concede £35m is outstanding to United World, but insist the debt is not behind the restructure. A spokesperson declined to comment after Wednesday’s hearing.

“Sheffield United Football Club is aware of today’s hearing at the high court,” read a club statement. “This is a matter between the current owners and former owner.”

Nevertheless, there could be ramifications for United. Under EFL regulations, any club official who is the subject of two insolvency events is prevented from acting as a controlling owner or director. In 2023, Rosen was a director of a US medical manufacturer, Invacare, that filed for bankruptcy, so he could be forced by the EFL to stand down and reduce his shareholding in United.

The EFL is also likely to launch a formal investigation into the allegations that the club’s owners are deliberately seeking to avoid paying fees owed from their purchase of the club, which would result in a points deduction if they are found guilty. EFL sources with knowledge of its rule book confirmed that an insolvency overseas would count as a disqualification event.

“The EFL notes the high court’s decision to issue a winding-up order on COH Sports Bidco Limited,” a spokesperson said. “The league will consider the implications of that development in line with its regulations, including whether any further action is required.

“In addition, the EFL continues to consider other regulatory matters following changes to the club’s ownership structure and developments within the wider group. As these issues remain ongoing, the EFL will make no further comment at this stage.”

United World claimed the club’s owners have refused repeated requests to reach a mediated settlement. “United World made every effort to resolve this matter amicably and tried until the morning of the hearing to give the owners a final opportunity to find a solution and spare Sheffield United the consequences of their conduct,” read a statement. “That approach, like everyone before it, received no response.

“It appears that Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen are simply not concerned about what this means for the club. What happens to Sheffield United now is the result of their choices.”

Sports.title: 'We tell him off if he gets carried away!': Brighton star JACK HINSHELWOOD joins dad Adam and great-uncle Martin to reflect on three generations of serving the Seagulls, the club's 'incredible' journey and his goal target for this season
Sports.content:
'We tell him off if he gets carried away!': Brighton star JACK HINSHELWOOD joins dad Adam and great-uncle Martin to reflect on three generations of serving the Seagulls, the club's 'incredible' journey and his goal target for this season

Unlock more of the best of our football coverage with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

Jack Hinshelwood's season ended with a flourish. There were the three goals in as many games as Brighton qualified for Europe and a distinct feeling there were more where they came from.

Hinshelwood, having first broken into the team at full back and played deep in midfield, has thrived as a high-energy No 10 in Fabian Hurzeler's side, forcing errors from those trying to pass their way out of defence and latching onto crosses to threaten the goal.

Thomas Tuchel liked what he saw and selected the 21-year-old in England's 55-man longlist for the World Cup. Wealthy Premier League rivals monitored his accelerated progress, too.

Summer speculation about interest from Arsenal sparked flattering online comparisons to David Platt, the former England captain with a reputation for scoring goals from midfield.

'If I'm going to play in this higher position, I want to start scoring a few more goals,' Hinshelwood tells Daily Mail Sport. 'I scored four last season but could have had 15 so I'm working hard to turn good positioning into more goals and assists. I want to score 10-plus if we're going to play 50-60 games.

'There's a lot to play for this season. We're in the Conference League, which is a massive target for us. We really want to do well in Europe. We'll be better prepared than two years ago. We want to go as far as we can, like in every competition.'

Hinshelwood discusses his ambitions under the critical gaze of his father Adam, a former Brighton player now manager of Worthing in the National League, and his great-uncle Martin, who has served Brighton in several coaching roles including as manager and director of football, and still scouts for the club.

Jack Hinshelwood, his father Adam (right) and great-uncle Martin (left) have all served Brighton with distinction as either a player or coach

The trio met Daily Mail Sport at Brighton Museum and Art Gallery, for the opening of a permanent exhibition tracing the history of the club

A talented and versatile player, Jack is entering his fourth season with the Brighton first team and has been touted for an England call-up

For all his confidence, Jack qualifies everything with regular promises not to look 'too far ahead' and to 'focus on Brighton' and let the rest take care of itself. His family background guards naturally against the dangers of getting carried away.

'He'll get told off by the rest of us if he does,' teases Martin but his expert eye tells him his great-nephew has the attributes required to turn this excellent start into an elite career.

'You're in a learning curve and it's a massive bonus if you're able to play in different areas of the pitch with the ability and the will to play there, because I know some players will go, "What you playing me there for? I don't want to play there. I want to play in that position".'

Martin expects Jack will eventually settle into central midfield. 'His awareness is his big asset,' says the 73-year-old. 'He knows where he is on the pitch and where others are. He sees things and does things early. He's just an intelligent footballer, probably more intelligent than any of the rest of us who have played.'

Three generations of the Hinshelwood family are together at Brighton Museum and Art Gallery for the opening of a permanent exhibition tracing the history of the club, and especially its revival since the closure of the Goldstone Ground amid fears of liquidation in 1997, from exile in Gillingham to success in the Premier League.

'The journey has been incredible,' says Jack, whose introduction came as an infant at the Withdean athletics complex where Brighton played home games after returning to the city in 1999. His father was in the team.

Likewise, Adam's early recollections include splashing around with his cousins in the huge communal baths inside the Goldstone dressing rooms when Martin worked on the staff. And later as ball boy at the Withdean as the team started its climb back to the top.

Martin, Adam and Jack have been witnesses to Brighton's 'incredible' journey from near extinction to European football

Jack is honoured alongside fellow Brighton fan favourites in the exhibition covering that revival

Brighton's former Withdean ground was a distinctive venue for football, with an athletics track around the pitch

'There was a buzz when the team came back to play in Brighton and Hove,' says Adam, 42. 'And there were back-to-back promotions and before you knew it the Withdean was a Championship ground hosting some big teams.

'It was layered differently to normal grounds. The players' lounge was a nursery by day and there was a pub literally inside the ground. Now they're building a pub inside the Amex so it'll bring some history back.'

The Hinshelwoods are woven into the club's fabric.

Adam, who is the son of Crystal Palace legend Paul, was thrust into the Brighton first team at the age of 18, making his debut on the opening day of the 2002-03 campaign when his uncle Martin was manager.

He was voted man of the match in a win at Burnley and then dropped for the next game. There was a call-up by England Under 21s but no cap before his progress was halted by a serious knee injury and he retired by the age of 26.

'My career was similar to Martin's,' says Adam. 'Dad would always tell me how good Martin was as a central midfielder who could do everything, score goals, create goals and stop goals.

'His career was cut short and he got into coaching and management, and I've been fortunate to do the same. We've been on the same path. That's why I've told Jack to do his coaching badges. He's working towards his UEFA B licence.'

'He's just an intelligent footballer,' says Martin of Jack. 'Probably more intelligent than any of the rest of us who has played'

Jack's dad Adam played over 100 games for Brighton between 2002 and 2009

Martin and Paul were sons of Wally Hinshelwood who played for seven clubs, most notably Reading and Bristol City in the 1950s.

They both graduated from the youth ranks at Crystal Palace in an exciting era when Malcolm Allison and Terry Venables were in charge at Selhurst Park.

Martin's professional playing career was curtailed by injury at the age of 24. Paul went on to make 319 appearances over 10 years at Palace, mostly as a right back despite starting out as a striker.

'Paul had that attitude,' recalls Martin. 'He was a striker who scored lots of goals and when they put him at right back he wasn't too keen, but he worked hard and ended up playing for England Under-21s.'

One of his two Under-21 caps came at the Goldstone, where his every touch was booed by a partisan Brighton crowd on a night when local hero Peter Ward scored three in a 6-0 win against Norway.

'There's no magic to it,' says Martin, as he attempts to explain the dynasty with a story about his father's matter-of-fact reaction to his release by Fulham at the age of 15.

'I came all the way home from Putney on my own. Train, bus, in through the front door and he went: "Are they taking you as an apprentice, then?" I said, "No". And he said: "You're probably not good enough". Then you think: "Well, I'll show you".

'My parents helped us in every way but always left a bit there to say, "Go on, you need to do more". That's how it's got to be or you can have a problem. I had that as a kid and Adam had that with his dad as well.

'They'd always find something in the game and go, "Hey, remember that?". You might have had a blinder, but they'd forget all the good things and remind you about that one thing. It's just to keep your feet on the ground and keep you wanting to improve and be a better person and player.'

Having played for rivals Crystal Palace, Martin stepped in as Brighton's caretaker manager on several occasions in the 2000s

'None of us are comfortable with what we've got,' says Jack. 'Like Dad in his coaching, he's doing really well but we all want more. It never stops'

As coaches with family in football, Martin and Adam find themselves doing the same thing.

'My youngest son is 11 and he probably gets it a lot easier than Jack did,' says Adam. 'When I started, I had my uncle coaching at Brighton and he'd shout to me: "Hinsh, are you all right?" and I'd say, "Yeah" and he'd say, "Liven up then". That would get to me every time.'

Jack has no complaints about the extra scrutiny. 'None of us are comfortable with what we've got,' he says. 'Like Dad in his coaching, he's doing really well but we all want more. It never stops.

'And probably that means we don't enjoy it sometimes as we should, but we always just want more.'

Brighton's new season starts tonight with a Conference League play-off tie against Tromso in Norway, before they host Aston Villa in the Premier League on Sunday. Expect more from young Hinshelwood.

Sports.title: 'He's not in it for the money': Insiders reveal the real reasons why football sceptic Jeff Bezos has bought into Liverpool - as well as his plans for his 'new toy', why Reds' commercial income will explode and angry fan groups' next steps
Sports.content:
'He's not in it for the money': Insiders reveal the real reasons why football sceptic Jeff Bezos has bought into Liverpool - as well as his plans for his 'new toy', why Reds' commercial income will explode and angry fan groups' next steps

Unlock more of the best of our journalism with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight and the writers you love every day

There's an old and barely documented story about Jeff Bezos that is worth excavating for a single reason – the yarn is the only one to suggest Liverpool’s newest shareholder held even a passing interest in sport as a child.

It dates to when Bezos, 62, was aged nine and living in Houston. As the mother to a bookish, scrawny lad, Jacklyn Bezos thought her boy needed to toughen up, which meant shifting him from his comfort zones of Star Trek and studying.

This would have been around 1973 and American football was the means to an end Jacklyn chose. In Texas, that is no small undertaking, so Jacklyn had her worries. ‘I thought he was going to get creamed out there,’ she said in the buried sections of an interview published by Wired in 1999.

Naturally, the profile didn’t conclude with a punchline about violent defeat. Instead, as Bezos’s late mother recalled it, the future founder of Amazon was the only child on the side capable of memorising all the plays. Not only his plays, but those of all his team-mates, too. She claimed he was made captain of the defence in the space of two weeks.

It’s a fun snippet but difficult to corroborate – Daily Mail Sport has trawled the archives of Houston’s multiple local newspapers from that period and found no mention of a ‘Coach Meisner’, which was among the few tangible details when the Washington Post – which Bezos now owns – repeated the anecdote in 2000. Emails to a couple of American football historians in Texas also proved fruitless.

If the story teaches us anything, it is the rarity of finding the young Bezos in any athletic environment whatsoever.

Jeff Bezos (pictured with his wife Lauren Sanchez), the world's third richest man, is part of a consortium that have bought almost 40 per cent of Liverpool

There is little evidence Bezos has any passion for sport, much less football - so why has he bought into Liverpool?

A young Bezos was encouraged by his mother to play American football in a bid to toughen him up - but we can't find any records of his sporting exploits

When Daily Mail Sport contacted his former school, Palmetto High in Miami, it required only six minutes to establish that the most famous of their alumni from the class of 82 never kicked, threw, jumped, swam, ran or sailed for any of its teams.

Wade Rowdon, once a third baseman at Cincinnati Reds and three years ahead of Bezos at Palmetto, told me he only recently found out they attended the same school – Bezos may have changed the world of retail forever but, evidently, he never left even the faintest of sporting footprints on his own playground.

All of which means nothing and something, because there are important questions to be asked of the ‘why’ whenever a financial behemoth lays hands on a sporting institution, and a deep-seated passion for the property at hand is often the first to be ruled out. In the case of Liverpool FC and its union with the world’s third richest man, that can be taken as a given.

A week has passed since Liverpool’s owners Fenway Sports Group (FSG) announced a ‘definitive agreement’ had been reached for a consortium named 1892 Holdings to buy a ‘minority’ stake in the club at the heart of a socialist city.

It has since transpired that the slice of the pie they have bought for more than £2billion is significantly bigger than initially reported – closer to 38 or 39 per cent rather than 30 per cent – and that options exist for 1892 to assume a majority shareholding within 12 months.

Daily Mail Sport has spoken to figures involved in the deal, financial experts and supporter groups concerned about the implications. But among the bigger mysteries within all of it is Bezos, a man worth £194.9billion, according to Forbes’ real-time listings on Wednesday morning.

Based on our conversations with individuals connected to the negotiations, Bezos was not on the frontline of talks, nor anywhere especially close. That role was taken by Amit Bhatia, the former co-owner of QPR and son-in-law of Indian steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal.

We understand Bhatia first met with FSG president Mike Gordon a year ago, after introductions from Will McDonough, the founder of Corestone Capital and a former agent to NFL legend Tom Brady. Interestingly, McDonough was also a senior adviser to the White House task force at this summer’s World Cup.

It was during the World Cup that FSG founder John W Henry is understood to have met Bhatia at an elite private members’ club in New York, Zero Bond, with the deal having moved quickly over the summer. ‘The past three months is when it all escalated,’ a source from the consortium told Daily Mail Sport.

Former QPR vice-chairman Amit Bhatia has been the face of the 1892 consortium, holding meetings with FSG president Mike Gordon a year ago

Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is also attached to the group, through his wife Elaine

It is well known by now that Bhatia will be abundantly visible as the vice-chair of the new Liverpool, pending approval of the acquisition by the independent regulator, and two more board seats will go to members of the 1892 consortium – Elaine Saverin, the wife of Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin, and Bryan Baum, who is the managing partner of K5 Global.

Bezos, the lead investor in K5, is conspicuous in that he holds no precise role and will instead hover as an unseen force in the background.

Our sources characterised him distinctly as a ‘silent partner’ and K5 is yet to reply to multiple Daily Mail Sport requests for clarity on the precise size of his investment, with K5 said to have pumped $1billion into the consortium’s coffers. With that level of attachment, it is safe to assume that if Bezos wishes to pull a string at the club, the absence of a designated board seat would be little more than a furniture issue.

And yet the opaque nature of his involvement, and a perceived lack of transparency around the wider process, is part of the uncertainty that has brought some anxiety to the fanbase.

Daily Mail Sport has been told the influential supporter group Spirit of Shankly (SoS) will hold a meeting with the regulator next week to share a few of those thoughts, which are inevitably tethered to memories of the despised ownership of George Gillett and Tom Hicks, which preceded FSG.

A spokesperson for SoS told Daily Mail Sport on Tuesday: ‘We want to know what it all means for Liverpool. We know firsthand what it's like to have bad ownership, so we want to know how the club will be run and by whom.’

The same spokesperson got in touch on Wednesday, after it emerged in The Athletic that the stake was closer to 40 per cent, adding: ‘The fact we didn’t know the percentage has given us more questions to ask. It has changed the landscape – this is not a small investment and we need to know more about what it means for the club.’

There is some reading to be done between the lines here. Change can be good, of course, and there is no one so blind as to assume FSG have lacked mis-steps since taking over for £300million in 2010 – they were part of the grubby posse that tried for a Super League breakaway and have pushed for an assortment of unpopular price hikes.

But FSG, while overseeing multiple sporting victories from their base in Boston, have also shown, on occasion, a willingness to listen to public backlashes, notably after the fury that erupted around their plans to raise ticket prices this year. The fans forced a rethink, but it’s a dynamic that cannot be guaranteed with new faces – the jokes about discussing supporter issues with an Amazon chatbot will no doubt write themselves.

Sources involved in the 1892 deal have stressed that they will engage the supporters, but said those conversations will likely occur after the regulator has approved the purchase. The intervening wait of up to 90 days could supply a vacuum for fraught sentiments, especially as Premier League and UEFA spending rules mean the era of free-spending on popular new signings are over.

Bezos has only ever been spotted at one football match - USA's defeat by Belgium at the World Cup last month

Liverpool fan group Spirit of Shankly, who protested the club's involvement in the Super League under FSG, want answers around the nature of Bezos' investment

Quite why Bezos is investing in Liverpool is both obvious and difficult to decipher. Returns in the best-case scenario would be pocket change to a man of his wealth, but iconic sporting properties are hard to acquire. By extension, they are attractive.

After backing away from explored purchases of the Seattle Seahawks and Washington Commanders in 2019 and 2023 respectively, Liverpool is Bezos’s entry point to an alien world.

It is understood that he hasn’t yet stepped foot inside Anfield and his appearance, alongside his wife Lauren Sanchez, at Team USA’s World Cup defeat by Belgium in Seattle last month is the only clear evidence of him ever attending a match. The assumption of Kieran Maguire, the noted football finance expert, is that Liverpool will serve as something akin to a fancy new toy, which might tally with the separate impression that Bezos has grown fonder of a celebrity lifestyle in the past decade.

‘Bezos isn't in it for the money because even if he makes $500million out of this himself, it's not going to move the dial for him,’ Maguire told me.

‘It’s about the kudos, I think. It's about being able to own a room in a different way at a cocktail party. Everybody in that set has an apartment in Manhattan, a yacht, there's only 20 football clubs in the Premier League and there's only one Liverpool. It could just be a hobby, a trophy asset.’

That might serve as scant comfort for Liverpool fans, who will be cognisant that the presence of Bezos is no guarantee of success – masses of discarded staff from the Washington Post prove that point.

But Maguire does foresee key areas of potential for Liverpool from the wider alliance, especially as a means of capitalising on the rapid, recent growth of Indian interest in the Premier League.

‘Longer term, what are Liverpool looking for?’ Maguire asks. ‘They're looking to expand into international markets under the cost-control rules and where are the growth opportunities? Answer A is the United States. Well, hello, Jeff Bezos. And answer B is India. Hello, Mr Mittal (whose family trust is named alongside Bhatia in the purchase).

‘I think there is the opportunity there to use the knowledge of those individuals to enable Liverpool to extract further commercial income, to tap into their networks, to tap into their expertise.

‘As for Bezos personally, my gut reaction is that it’s a vanity purchase, but as a secondary thought, he will want to expand Amazon into new markets and having an involvement with an iconic club will help.’

'It's about being able to own a room at a cocktail party. Everybody in that set has an apartment in Manhattan, a yacht, but there's only one Liverpool'

Time will tell if that leads one day to Amazon sponsorship on the shirt or stadium wall – sources in the deal claim it was not part of the current thinking. We also understand there is no concern from the Premier League or UEFA about perceived conflicts of interest around Amazon Prime’s ownership of broadcasting rights to football. Precedents already exist in that area.

That said, there is a mild curiosity, expressed by one figure near the top of British football, about whether this involvement might encourage Bezos to put extra effort into tackling rights piracy, which is often linked to modified Amazon Fire Sticks.

For now, that is an unknown. So too is the question of whether Bezos might be faced with a rush of cancelled subscriptions if results go badly or fans dislike what they discover.

It might not go in that direction, of course, but football can be funny like that. Presumably Bezos has learned as much in his due diligence, because 53 years after he pulled on pads for a kids’ team, there are myriad ways he could still get creamed.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick has been set up to fail by Ineos - but it's not the first time he's been let down by his bosses. This is the proof he's the perfect manager for Man United's threadbare squad
Sports.content:
When Michael Carrick’s star was in its ascendancy at Middlesbrough, with first-season performances at places like Sheffield United and Burnley which were described as ‘near perfection’ creating a genuine prospect of promotion to the Premier League, he was being compared by some to Keanu Reeves' character in The Matrix. A quiet and immensely self-possessed individual using all his mental faculties to navigate a manic universe.

He likes to say that being a former midfielder influences the way he coaches – it’s not all blood and thunder with him – and if one word encapsulates the way he worked on Teesside, then it is ‘calm’.

But his mentor Sir Alex Ferguson once said that there are times in football management where ‘you have to stand up for yourself – there is no other way’. Carrick’s disinclination to do that struck many at the start of a second season at the Middlesbrough helm, as he struggled to live up to the big reputation he had built in his first.

No fewer than 14 senior players had left in that summer’s transfer window, including forwards Chuba Akpom and Cameron Archer, as Boro ended a heavy dependency on loan signings.

Carrick, left to assimilate new recruits and build a new team on the hoof for a fanbase expecting another promotion push, was plunged into undoubtedly his toughest period in football. Boro picked up two points from their winless first seven games and after a desultory Tuesday night draw at Sheffield Wednesday – where they trailed at half-time – sat rock bottom.

Those bleak, winless months looked like second season syndrome – a time, if ever there was one, for him to speak up, defend himself and send a veiled message ‘upstairs’. Nothing of the sort was forthcoming, as Carrick, steadfastly disinclined to use the press conference sphere for his own purposes as Ferguson always would, remained a rock-solid company man.

Man United's lack of transfer business means Michael Carrick has been set up to fail before a ball has even been kicked this season

But Carrick has been here before going into his second season - he lost 14 senior players in the equivalent summer at Middlesbrough, including star striker Chuba Akpom (second from right)

As he prepares Manchester United for the new campaign, Carrick does not have another full-scale rebuild on his hands, but he is once again entitled to feel the sting of indignation about how he is being sent into a second season by his employers.

The landscape is wholly different to his first United season, with the return of Champions League football likely to mean United will play 15 games more. Yet to date, they have just two significant additions to what was already a thin squad: Youri Tielemans, a 29-year-old with many miles on the clock, and Andrey Santos, a recruit from Chelsea nowhere near the finished article.

Ahead of Saturday’s opening game at Hull, Carrick has the same old dependency on Luke Shaw, who is nowhere near capable of playing the two games per week which European football demands, and the other defensive old-stager Harry Maguire.

Matthijs de Ligt has not played a game since last November. Lisandro Martinez is recovering from a thigh problem after an injury-ravaged last season. Benjamin Sesko has not kicked a ball in pre-season. There is, as yet, no one new to energise a midfield from which Casemiro has gone and Manuel Ugarte will be missing most of the season. United have a lower summer spend than Ipswich Town and Coventry City.

It feels like Carrick is being set up to fail before a ball is even kicked, with some analysts already inferring that he is not the man to take United on. Jamie Carragher recently suggested that he lacks the ‘stardust’ to win them a Premier League or Champions League title.

Having rescued United from the humiliating position that the club’s owners, Ineos, found themselves in after begging the incapable and tempestuous Ruben Amorim to leave Sporting Lisbon to manage their club, Carrick deserves much better. Yet for all that, the evidence of the pre-season tells us that he is the same safe, dependable guy who didn't make waves at Middlesbrough.

If you looked hard enough, there were signs of a man trying to send a message that he needed more players, as he sat in a hotel meeting room with national print journalists at Manchester United’s hotel in County Kildare after the recent friendly against Leeds United. ‘We've got to keep pushing, really, and push everything in every boundary that we can, to be able to win again,’ he said.

But he’s agreed to Amazon camera crews being around the club for a United documentary series – something no United manager before him would ever have countenanced, least of all Amorim, with his predilection for punching TVs.

Carrick's options for Saturday's game against Hull are far from ideal - striker Benjamin Sesko, for example, has not featured throughout pre-season

United still depend on left back Luke Shaw, who is nowhere near capable of playing the two games per week which European football demands

He’s said it’s acceptable that United, whose commercial revenues are the second highest in world football, won’t pursue £100million players, despite the club being the only one of the ‘Big Six’ not to have done so. He hasn’t even brought up the question of the season’s significantly greater workload.

While some afford Carrick the public indignities they would be less willing to submit a foreign manager to, the Manchester United faithful are desperate for him to be the one who brings the club out of the post-Ferguson purgatory.

Ineos and their United chief executive Omar Berrada have made grand boasts about ‘Project 150’ – winning or challenging for the Premier League by the club’s 150th anniversary in 2028 – which will come back to bite fans if unaccomplished. Ineos, not Carrick, will be on the receiving end of supporters’ opprobrium if this becomes another turbulent season.

For the many who want to see Carrick flourish, there is evidence from that second Middlesbrough season of how his understated and thoughtful approach might just deliver.

Those who viewed him at close quarters still remember that steadfast loyalty to the owners. ‘There was never any sign of him rocking the boat,’ says Dominic Shaw, who covers the club for The Northern Echo. ‘Even through that winless stretch, he went nowhere near suggesting, “I don’t yet have the squad”.’

Asked before leaving Hillsborough, on the nadir of a night which kept them bottom, what he had told his players at half-time, Carrick inevitably replied: ‘I kept calm.’ But many of the players who came through the difficult early months to find success and finish eighth in that 2023-24 season speak of how his application to the small details of their technique made them better players, in the eye of that storm.

Morgan Rogers, who’d struggled to convince in a number of loan moves when he arrived at Boro in July 2023, spoke when eventually called up by England of how Carrick had been a ‘massive part’ in his own development. ‘He gave me the confidence to express myself.’

Carrick called him to thank him for these words but told him: ‘Don't play down how much you've done yourself.’ For Rogers, management, in the purest sense of the word, had clearly mattered more than that amorphous ‘stardust’ quality which pundits speak of. Humility is a part of it. It’s thought that Carrick did not try to bring his own decorated playing career into his conversations with Rogers.

England star and Chelsea summer signing Morgan Rogers credits Carrick as being a 'massive part' of his development

It felt significant in a recent County Kildare discussion with journalists that Carrick did not take the chance offered to him to say he felt ‘empathy’ for Marcus Rashford

Rogers would repay Boro with a £15million profit in his move to Aston Villa, having dazzled in the club’s run to the Carabao Cup semi-final. Emmanuel Latte Lath, also signed that summer, turned out to be the Championship’s striker of the season and Rav van den Berg, now playing in the Bundesliga, proved an excellent centre back. Boro eventually profited to the tune of around £50million from that summer's buys.

A source who knows Lath tells of how Carrick managed to drop the striker to the bench without jolting the confidence which so many forwards feed off. Van den Berg speaks of Carrick’s ‘understanding’ of what it was taking to adjust to the Championship.

Carrick’s presence on a Zoom call had been instrumental to him signing. Yet there was clearly an uncompromising side to him on Teesside. ‘It was not all sweetness and light. It’s a hard game and his dressing room reflected that,’ says the source close to Lath.

It felt significant in the County Kildare discussion with journalists that Carrick did not take the chance offered to him to say he felt ‘empathy’ for Marcus Rashford. Perhaps this was Carrick code for ‘grow up and sort yourself out’. But all the soundings suggest he is ready to give the forward the fresh start Amorim would not countenance for the England international.

Carrick’s tone seemed different when it came to Kobbie Mainoo, another cast to the margins by Amorim. He and Mainoo have been in touch on and off throughout his frustrating summer with England. Carrick didn’t discuss Amad Diallo in Ireland but he is another young United player thought to feel reinvigorated. Echoes of that Boro cohort.

Carrick’s most questionable act at Middlesbrough was a decision to replace first-team coach Aaron Danks with his own brother Graeme, previously the Newcastle United Under 18s coach, when Danks left to join Vincent Kompany at Bayern Munich.

But the appointment of Danks, within two months of his own appointment, did underline Carrick’s ability to assemble a good ‘brains trust’. At United, Steve Holland has become the same problem-solver and shrewd tactician with answers that Gareth Southgate always found him to be with England.

Carrick was aware from day one that the fragility in this United group was borne of the chaotic changes Amorim would make, half an hour before kick-off. Holland is there to make sure everything is clear. Jonathan Woodgate and Jonny Evans, who make up the coaching team, are popular. It is the strongest and most united backroom team for many seasons.

Carrick left Teesside with a reputation for predictability: being bound to an aesthetically pleasing pass-and-move style with ‘only one distinct way of playing’ as Sunderland’s extremely adaptable and dynamic manager Regis Le Bris brutally described the team down the A19 after beating them in 2024.

Carrick left Teesside with a reputation for predictability: being bound to an aesthetically pleasing pass-and-move style with ‘only one distinct way of playing’

But United's pursuit of the tough defensive midfielder Carlos Baleba (right) suggests Carrick has learned from his mistakes

‘They were not as streetwise as they needed to be,’ says the Northern Echo’s Shaw. ‘Being unable to see games out was a repeated problem and there was also a sequence of conceding shambolic goals through poor defending.’

There is evidence that Carrick has learned from that experience, too. The pursuit of tough central and defensive midfielder Carlos Baleba from Brighton would, if it comes off, suggest a big shift from his old aesthetic.

The season ahead will bring United up against some of those players Carrick mentored so well at Middlesbrough. They will face Morgan Rogers at Chelsea, two months from now. Akpom, transformed in Carrick's first season, is on the fringes of the Ipswich side the team meet a week on Sunday.

Sitting back in that hotel meeting room to discuss the season ahead, the United manager pointedly dodged the question of whether his side can challenge for the title.

‘What we've done gives us the confidence to move forward. How quickly we keep moving forward, that's the challenge – but as long as we're stable and we can keep moving in the direction, I think that's what we can ask,' he stated.

He was as calm, unflustered and equable as always, but will need every ounce of skill to tackle the Matrix which lies ahead this time.

Sports.title: Inside the explosive WhatsApps about alleged Sydney Swans hotel incident: What's NOT true in texts and graphic photo going viral
Sports.content:
Sydney Swans WAGs appear to be battening down the hatches after the alleged hotel incident engulfing the team just days out from the AFL finals.

Isaac Heeney's fiancée Steffanie Waters and Chad Warner's long-term girlfriend Alice Hughes have both made telling changes to their social media accounts following the explosive allegations.

Heeney appears to have switched off comments on his Instagram account, while his bride-to-be has disabled comments on most posts.

Ms Waters' profile remains public, however, which is perhaps unsurprising given her career as an influencer.

Warner's girlfriend Ms Hughes, a Perth-raised nurse who moved to Sydney after the midfielder was drafted by the Swans, has made her Instagram account private.

The social media lockdown comes as the club finds itself at the centre of a police investigation just days before the AFL finals.

Isaac Heeney's fiancée Steffanie Waters disabled comments for most posts on her Instagram

It is possible that Waters' account only remains public due to her work as an influencer

Chad Warner voluntarily spoke with police about the allegations but was not arrested. He is pictured here with his long-term girlfriend Alice Hughes

The Swans were celebrating a crucial 36-point victory over Essendon at the MCG on Sunday, a result which cemented second spot on the ladder and booked them a home qualifying final at the SCG.

But by Monday morning, the mood had dramatically changed.

Victoria Police attended the Pullman East Melbourne hotel, where the Swans had been staying, following a report of an alleged sexual assault in the early hours of the morning.

And amid the police investigation, a series of questionable WhatsApp messages purporting to reveal what unfolded inside the Melbourne hotel have been doing the rounds online.

The messages, which the Mail has not been able to independently authenticate, make a string of extraordinary claims about the events that allegedly took place after the Swans' victory on Sunday.

However, key inconsistencies raise serious doubts about the authenticity and veracity of the texts.

According to the messages, Warner, Heeney, Riley Bice, James Jordon and a fifth unnamed player were 'all in custody'.

However, this cannot be true because the players were not arrested, voluntarily offered their assistance to the police investigation, and returned to Sydney via rental car.

Victoria Police attended the Pullman East Melbourne hotel (pictured), where the Swans had been staying, following a report of an alleged sexual assault in the early hours of the morning

The unverified messages make a string of extraordinary claims about the events that allegedly took place after the Swans' victory on Sunday. The players were not arrested and were able to leave the state and return to Sydney via rental car

An unauthenticated text purports to show an image from inside the Pullman hotel

A photo circulating online has already been debunked as a fake

One bizarre message alleges how a woman was injured in the room, with a photo offered as evidence. However, that image has already been debunked as a fake taken months ago.

Screenshots of the texts also make wild and entirely unverified claims of a woman taunting a player with insects, only for an argument to erupt, causing damage to the hotel, while another player allegedly took bets on the ensuing chaos.

There is no evidence to suggest this account of the incident is true.

And, as if the tale needed another twist, a separate message seen by the Mail claims that three women were seen leaving the Pullman lobby, with one allegedly telling those around her she had 'recorded' events inside the room.

Club staff were reportedly overheard telling the women they were not aware of any alleged incident, before a third woman arrived at the hotel to help her friends.

Witnesses claimed two women had approached hotel staff at about 7am on Monday asking to be allowed into a guest room.

One of the women was reportedly 'hysterical'.

The women allegedly became agitated when staff told them they could not return to the room and confronted team officials, including coach Dean Cox, in the foyer.

Witnesses said Cox appeared stunned by the confrontation.

The upset woman was then reportedly seen running to a hotel bathroom in tears shortly before police were called.

Riley Bice was recruited to the Sydney Swans in 2024

James Jordon of the Swans is seen warming up before a game on July 9

But amid the increasingly lurid claims, there is one important caveat: none of the claims contained in the messages have been confirmed by police, the club or those allegedly involved.

The Mail does not suggest the messages provide an accurate account of events.

Victoria Police detectives from the Sexual Crimes Squad are investigating a report of an alleged sexual assault in East Melbourne on August 17.

Police said the incident occurred at a hotel on Wellington Parade in the early hours of Monday morning.

'The exact circumstances are yet to be established and the investigation into the incident remains ongoing,' a Victoria Police spokesperson said.

'Police spoke to a number of people at the hotel, however no one has been arrested or formally interviewed at this time.'

Detectives have since requested CCTV from the hotel as they work to establish exactly what occurred.

The AFL Integrity Unit has also launched an investigation into the alleged incident.

The Swans have confirmed multiple players were involved in an alleged incident and said they were working with the AFL and relevant authorities.

Swans CEO Matthew Pavlich said the club understood there would be intense interest in the matter but urged people to wait for the facts.

'We understand the level of interest in the matter and there is going to be lots of speculation,' he said.

'But given it is a police matter right now, that is all that we can say.'

Coach Dean Cox broke his silence on Tuesday morning, expressing his bitter disappointment as the club was plunged into crisis just days before the finals.

Cox was grilled by television reporters as he arrived at Swans headquarters in Moore Park shortly after 7am for crisis talks.

'Yeah, obviously extremely disappointed with what's happened and I understand the questions,' he said.

'We'll update as we gather more information.'

Club officials are now considering whether players allegedly involved should be stood down from Sunday's final-round clash against North Melbourne, with any sanctions potentially extending into the finals.

The prospect of losing several of their biggest stars could have enormous ramifications for the Swans' premiership campaign.

Cox said the club was working through the situation with the AFL and other relevant parties.

Asked whether he had spoken to his players, Cox replied: 'We'll speak as the day unfolds.'

The coach had earlier admitted the club was still trying to piece together exactly what had happened.

'We're still piecing together exactly what has transpired here and have our own set of internal enquiries ongoing,' he said on Monday.

'But it's safe to say we're extremely shocked and disappointed.'

Police spoke to Heeney, Warner, Bice, Jordon and a fifth unnamed player on Monday before they returned to Sydney. No charges have been laid.

The Mail does not suggest any of those players are under investigation or involved in any wrongdoing, but merely that they spoke to police in connection with the alleged incident.

The club has also launched an internal investigation into claims that players were out late in Melbourne drinking alcohol until after midnight.

That could potentially result in additional sanctions, separate to the police investigation.

Sports.title: Tottenham push on with moves for City duo Marmoush and Savinho, Aston Villa face competition for Tosin Adarabioyo... and Newcastle are offered former Blues forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Inter confident Jones will have medical Inter Milan expect Curtis Jones to be cleared to have a medical today ahead of a £30.7million move from Liverpool. Inter have bid £26.7m plus £4m in add-ons with a 10 per cent sell-on clause, offering a similar structure to the deal used to sign Djed Spence from Tottenham. Jones will sign a five-year deal with the Italian champions if the transfer is agreed. Napoli ask about Jackson Napoli have made an enquiry for Chelsea forward Nicolas Jackson with Arsenal’s Gabriel Jesus reluctant to make the move. Nicolas Jackson could leave Chelsea this summer Clarets agree deal for Ahmedhodzic Burnley have had a bid accepted by Feyenoord for centre-back Anel Ahmedhodzic. Southampton and his former club Sheffield United had also expressed an interest in the 27-year-old. Palace say no to Sarr approach Crystal Palace have rejected an approach of more than £30m from Galatasaray for Ismaila Sarr. Palace are also braced for offers for Adam Wharton. BOBBY MANZI Wrexham aim high with look at Leeds star Lucas Wrexham are showing interest in an ambitious move for Leeds United forward Lukas Nmecha. The 27-year-old joined Leeds last summer from Wolfsburg and scored seven goals in 37 appearances. The Welsh side are also exploring a deal for free agent centre-back and Congo international Axel Tuanzebe. Spurs push on with Marmoush and Savinho swoops Tottenham are continuing negotiations with Manchester City over the double deal of Savinho and Omar Marmoush. The fee for both would likely total around £140m. As Daily Mail Sport previously revealed, Spurs have identified the Brazilian winger and Egyptian forward as two targets for their forward line along with Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo. The deal with City would not be cheap, however, while coach Enzo Maresca also wants to ensure he has enough bodies with Jeremy Doku out for the start of the season. Liverpool, meanwhile, need to ensure they strengthen their own attacking options before allowing anyone to leave and would want a considerable fee to even consider selling Gakpo. Tottenham have made their interest known. Omar Marmoush is subject of a double swoop from Spurs along with Savinho Villa and Marseille keen on Chelsea's Tosin - after he loses No4 shirt Aston Villa hold interest in Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo but face competition from Marseille. Adarabioyo is one of a number of options being considered by Unai Emery. The 6ft 5ins centre-back had been willing to stay at Stamford Bridge and fight for his place but it is becoming apparent it would be in his career's best interests to explore a move away where he would have a more prominent role. Villa have been assessing names throughout the window after it became clear Arsenal would pursue Ezri Konsa who is likely to wrap up his £51m move to the champions by the weekend. Adarabioyo also has other other clubs to consider. Marseille have made contact with Chelsea and are deemed most likely to pursue a move as it stands. Tosin Adarabioyo signs a shirt for a fan in Hong Kong on Chelsea's pre-season tour Sevilla are also keen as are Marco Silva's Benfica but are not considered as strong as Marseille and Villa. Other clubs are also now showing interest in the 28-year-old who joined as a free agent after leaving Fulham in 2024. In another ominous sign, Adarabioyo has also lost his shirt number in a squad list reshuffle. Formerly No 4, Adarabioyo will now wear No 38. New signing Valentin Barco takes his old shirt. Liam Delap is no longer No 9 and will wear No 12,with Joao Pedro taking the No 9. Chslsea bag Hearts' Osborne Chelsea have signed 17-year-old centre-back Alfie Osborne from Hearts for £400,000. Osborne captained Hearts’ U18s to the Scottish FA Youth Cup and has also captained Scotland's U19s. Reijnders seals Saudi move Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has joined Al Qadsiah for £52m. Reijnders will work under Brendan Rodgers at Al Qadsiah. The 28-year-old, who has an offer from Nottingham Forest also, only joined City from AC Milan last summer for £46.3m and made 50 appearances, scoring seven goals. Tijjani Reijnders is leaving Manchester City after just one season Clarets land Coudet Burnley have signed goalkeeper Gregoire Coudet from French side Brest on a permanent deal. The 27-year-old has signed a four-year contract. Norwich City have signed Fenerbahce winger Anthony Musaba on a season's loan. The Championship club will pay a proportion of the 25-year-old's salary after finding a replacement for Ali Ahmed following his knee injury. Toffees consider Cash grab Everton are showing interest in Aston Villa right back Matty Cash as they assess all options in the market. Villa are signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka from West Ham today and he is being brought in to increase competition for Cash in the right-back berth. Poland international Cash has three years left on contract. Everton have been working through a raft of names to try and solve their issue at right-back which has even prompted questions from Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Barca keep tabs on Kane Barcelona are monitoring Harry Kane's contract talks with Bayern Munich. The England captain is giving priority to resolving his future with the German champions where he is settled and discussions are ongoing about the length of deal for the 33-year-old. Kane is understood to want a three year deal and, as Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this summer, Barca have made their interest known. Read the full story here. Villa braced for another Watkins bid Aston Villa anticipate a fourth bid from Al Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins. The England international is open to the move but so far Villa have rejected their advances and want to keep the 30-year-old. Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is understood to be open to a move to Saudi Arabia The latest bid of £38m was rejected on Tuesday evening. Villa maintain interested in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have confirmed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki. Left back Ruggeri, 24, joins from Atletico Madrid, while goalkeeper Suzuki, 23, arrives after two years in Italy with Parma. Meanwhile, Rangers have signed right back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Villa. The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy, which will be triggered by the number of games he plays. As Daily Mail Sport revealed last week, Villa are signing Aaron Wan Bissaka on loan from West Ham pending his medical today. The deal can become an obligation to buy at around £18million. There's a new Cherif in town Coventry have completed their ninth signing of the summer transfer window with Fenerbahce striker Sidiki Cherif for £20.5million. The deal has taken the club's spending to over £120m. The 19-year-old, who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January, made appearances in the Europa League and in this season’s Champions League qualifiers prior to opening talks with Coventry. Toon's Nkunku offer Newcastle have been offered the chance to sign former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku from AC Milan. However, their priority remains to sign a midfielder first hence talks with Man City for Nico Gonzalez. Other targets are also being discussed. Nkunku has been told he can leave Milan and has interest from RB Leipzig among others. ... and they're closing in on Diabate Newcastle are also closing on Genclerbirligi’s midfielder Ousmane Diabate. The highly-rated 18-year-old had been set for Brentford while Tottenham had also shown interest. However, Newcastle look to have won the race with the teenager likely to stay on loan in Turkey for another season. Diabate, a defensive midfielder, has played 10 matches for the U19s and seven for Genclerbirligi’s first team so far. Liverpool defensive prospect in talks over La Liga move Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is in talks to join Levante on loan. The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England so is having to be loaned out. The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future. First team football in a top league such as La Liga is viewed as an integral next step. He also has interest from Portugal and Germany. Winger Kieran Morrison is joining Sheffield Wednesday on loan today. Liverpool continue to discuss a move for Bradley Barcola at Paris St Germain but a deal for his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye is unlikely. Konsa nearing Arsenal move... Arsenal have agreed a £51million deal plus add-ons for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa. The England international has said goodbyes to staff at Villa and is due to undergo a medical tomorrow. Read the full story here. ...as Gunners seek deal for United youngster Arsenal are also working on a deal for 20-year-old right back Habeeb Ogunneye from Manchester United. Arsenal want players to boost their U21s squad and have also shown interest in United's James Scanlon. Gibraltar international winger Scanlon was on loan at Swindon Town last season. England youth international Ogunneye had a spell at Newport on loan. Baleba close to United switch Manchester United are closing on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba. Talks resumed for the Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became apparent his ankle ligament injury was not as serious as first feared. Read the full story here. Pogba tears up Monaco deal Monaco have confirmed that Paul Pogba has left by mutual agreement, bringing his time at the Ligue 1 club to a premature end. The 33-year-old former Manchester United midfielder is now a free agent and has been offered to clubs in the MLS. Read the full story here. Paul Pogba's time at Monaco is over - with MLS clubs now considering a move for the former Man United midfielder Farke reunites with Elvedi Leeds have signed Nico Elvedi from Borussia Monchengladbach. The final fee is £6.5m rising to £8.5m with bonuses. The 29-year-old Switzerland international centre back worked with Daniel Farke previously at the Bundesliga club. James set for Wolves move Rennes midfielder Jordan James is poised to finalise his move to Wolves today pending his medical. The Wales international midfielder is joining on an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for around £10m. He impressed on loan at Leicester last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games and had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham. Chelsea defender closes on Italy move Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has arrived at Villa Stuart in Rome ahead of his medical this morning. The 25-year-old centre back is joining Napoli on loan for around £2.5m with an option for the deal to become permanent at £23m. Mamadou Sarr, meanwhile, is emerging as a target for Real Sociedad and Al Hilal. The 20-year-old has been expected to go on loan in the Premier League and interest there remains. The Senegal international was recalled from a loan at Strasbourg to provide cover last season and started in their FA Cup win over Hull. Piroe party at West Ham West Ham have signed Joel Piroe on loan from Leeds until the end of the season. The deal also includes an option for it to become permanent, which will be activated should certain conditions be met, including West Ham winning promotion back to the Premier League. Joel Piroe has joined West Ham on loan from Leeds West Ham turned to 27-year-old Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott who is joining Real Betis for £17m plus add ons. Piroe, who has scored 73 goals in the Championship during spells with Leeds and Swansea , said: 'I see West Ham as a Club that really wants to be in the Premier League, and I think should be in the Premier League. 'With my experience, I think I can help the Club a lot to achieve what they want to achieve, and I think it’s a good opportunity for me to show what I’ve learnt and how I’ve grown as a football player over the years.' Piroe finished the 2024-25 season as the Championship's top scorer, helping Leeds United earn promotion to the Premier League. The Hammers remain an option for free agent Jamie Vardy. Potters snare Ipswich pair Stoke have agreed a fee of around £6million with Ipswich for striker George Hirst and are also taking Ipswich full back Ben Johnson on loan. Scotland international Hirst is to undergo medical later today. The fee will increase on performance related bonuses. TUESDAY: Crystal Palace land £11m American star MONDAY: Liverpool unlikely to pursue PSG's Ibrahim Mbaye SUNDAY: Juventus reopen talks for Spurs keeper Vicario SATURDAY: Aston Villa in talks with Japan goalkeeper Zion Suzuki FRIDAY: Djed Spence completes £30million move to Inter Milan THURSDAY: Chelsea waiting for Fernandez bid WEDNESDAY: Man United target Carlos Baleba on Newcastle's radar TUESDAY: Roy Keane's son-in-law linked with move to Portugal
